display_title: Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

head_commit.message:
Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

`ClientLibrary::GetOrCreateLocalClient` previously keyed `local_instances_` only on `platform->id()`, ignoring `options.allowed_devices()` on cache hits. When multiple `PjRtClient` instances (or TensorFlow and PJRT clients) were created in the same process with different `allowed_devices` sets, every call after the first received the first call's `LocalClient` and its `StreamExecutor` list.

Therefore this change keys `ClientLibrary::local_instances_` by `(platform->id(), options.allowed_devices())` so each `allowed_devices` configuration gets a `LocalClient` restricted to those devices, while `DestroyLocalInstance(platform)` still clears all cached instances for that platform. It also:
- Updates `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient::UpdateCompileOptions` to fall back to `client()->default_device_ordinal()` instead of hardcoding device ordinal `0`, which fails when `allowed_devices` does not include device `0`.
- Forwards `visible_devices` in `GetTargetConfigFromOptions` (`xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_gpu_internal.cc`) when creating a GPU topology description via the PJRT C API.
- Preserves `allowed_devices` in `XlaDevice::Metadata` when looking up the `LocalClient`.

display_title: [XLA] Replace `InstructionFusion::IsEmbeddedComputation` with `CallGraph`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Replace `InstructionFusion::IsEmbeddedComputation` with `CallGraph`.

Whether a computation is embedded cannot be determined from its direct callers
alone: a `while`, `conditional`, or `call` body inside a `map`, `sort`, or
`reduce` has a `CallContext::kControlFlow` direct caller even though it executes
inside an embedded computation. `CallGraph` already computes transitive
`CallContext` in one pass over the module.

- Use `CallGraph` in `InstructionFusion`, `MultiOutputFusion`, and
  `EmbeddedWhileLoopUnroller`, checking specifically for
  `CallContext::kEmbedded` or `CallContext::kBoth` instead of calling
  `InstructionFusion::IsEmbeddedComputation`.
- Add `ScatterExpander::kEliminateEmbeddedScatters` backed by `CallGraph` and
  use it in `CpuCompiler` so transitively embedded scatters are expanded too.
- Remove `InstructionFusion::IsEmbeddedComputation`.

display_title: [XLA] Do not inline `map` computations rooted at control-flow instructions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Do not inline `map` computations rooted at control-flow instructions.

`MapInliner` currently skips `kFusion` roots when all operands are parameters,
but still tries to clone control-flow roots (`CallContext::kControlFlow`, such
as `kWhile`, `kConditional`, and `kCall`) directly to the tensor shape of the
enclosing `map`. Cloning those instructions to a non-scalar shape produces
invalid HLO (and for `while`, tensor-wide loop termination does not match
per-element `map` semantics). Skip inlining them as well.

display_title: Compile CUDA command buffer kernels to CUBIN via embeddable_cuda_library

head_commit.message:
Compile CUDA command buffer kernels to CUBIN via embeddable_cuda_library

`command_buffer_kernels.cc` previously embedded `.target sm_50` PTX strings for `set_case_condition`, `set_while_condition`, and `noop`. On the first conditional command buffer recording per device, `CudaExecutor::LoadModuleFromPtx` JIT-compiled that PTX on the single-threaded `cuda_driver` pool, stalling first recording by ~187 ms on `sm_103a` and serializing compilation across GPUs.

So this change compiles `SetCaseCondition`, `SetWhileCondition`, and `NoOp` as CUDA C++ kernels in `command_buffer_kernels.cu.cc` using `embeddable_cuda_library` (with `register_with_cudart = False` so `libcudart` never registers or eagerly loads the fatbinary on drivers older than CUDA 12.3) and resolves their `KernelLoaderSpec`s via `FindCudaRuntimeKernel`. This returns in-memory CUBIN specs that `CudaExecutor::LoadKernel` loads directly via `LoadModuleFromCuBin` (`LoadCubin`), avoiding both the single-threaded PTX driver JIT and `cudaGetFuncBySymbol`.

display_title: [XLA] Remove unnecessary `CallContext::kControlFlow` checks in `HloLivenessAnalysis`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Remove unnecessary `CallContext::kControlFlow` checks in `HloLivenessAnalysis`.

`PropagateLivenessToParameterCallers` and `PropagateLivenessThroughControlFlow`
already check each caller instruction's opcode (`kWhile`, `kCall`,
`kConditional`), so gating them on
`call_graph_node.context() == CallContext::kControlFlow` had no reason to be
there. Worse, when a `while`, `call`, or `conditional` is nested inside an
embedded computation such as `map`, `CallGraph` marks its callee computations
`CallContext::kEmbedded` (or `kBoth` if shared), so the check suppressed
liveness propagation to the caller and let `HloModuleDCE` treat live
loop-carried tuple elements as dead.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fix element count truncation when emitting large constants

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix element count truncation when emitting large constants

`ThunkEmitter::EmitConstant` stored the number of elements of a constant in an
`int`. For constants with 2^31 or more elements the count wrapped around, so
such a constant could be mistaken for a scalar: its global was sized as the
64 byte minimum allocation and `AppendGlobalConstant` copied the whole
content into the fixed 64 byte padding buffer, writing past its end.

Keep the element count as `int64_t`, so that only constants with at most one
element get an inline initializer, and only fill the padding buffer when the
content is actually smaller than the minimum allocation.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [CHLO] Do not recompose composites with a mismatched region count

head_commit.message:
[CHLO] Do not recompose composites with a mismatched region count

`ChloOpRecomposePattern` moves the regions of a `stablehlo.composite` into the
CHLO op it creates by zipping both region lists with `llvm::zip_equal`.
`stablehlo.composite` accepts any number of regions, while the CHLO ops have a
fixed number, and nothing checked that the two agree. `zip_equal` only asserts
on equal lengths; without assertions it iterates over the composite's regions,
so a composite with more regions than the CHLO op made the pattern access
regions past the end of the new op, and one with fewer left the new op with an
empty region.

Compare the region counts before moving the regions and fail the match when
they differ, erasing the op that was just created so the IR is left unchanged.
Such a composite is then left in place, like any other composite that the
pass does not recompose.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019015280

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add tiling space and tile propagation for single-indexed gather

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add tiling space and tile propagation for single-indexed gather

`TilingSpace` now registers a runtime variable for the start index of a gather
with a single indexed dimension and no batching dimensions
(`TilingSpace::ProcessGather`), and `PropagateTileToInput` propagates a gather
output tile to its operands (`PropagateTileToInputForGatherOp`):
- `start_indices` gets the batch dimension tiles of the output (which must have
  size 1; their stride is normalized to 1) and a size-1 tile for
  `index_vector_dim`; this one-element tile defines the runtime variable.
- The gathered operand gets size-1 tiles on `collapsed_slice_dims`, the offset
  dimension tiles of the output on the other dimensions, and its indexed
  dimension is shifted by the runtime variable.
Unsupported gathers (several indexed dimensions, batching dimensions, sub-byte
types, unsigned index types, batch tiles larger than 1) return Unimplemented.

This is NFC for production: gather is still unsupported by the Triton support
checks, and every pass that tiles a fusion checks Triton support first (or only
sees fusions that are already Triton fusions); the CPU tiled emitter rejects
gather in `IsSupportedTiledFusion` before tiling.

display_title: PR #52725: [XLA:GPU] Expose ROCm's libhipcxx from include/hipccl as its own include root

head_commit.message:
PR #52725: [XLA:GPU] Expose ROCm's libhipcxx from include/hipccl as its own include root

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52725

Motivation
As part of the move to the CCCL 3.0-3.3 API, AMD is introducing hipCCL, a
unified package for rocPRIM, hipCUB and rocThrust that mirrors the role
NVIDIA's CCCL plays for CUB, Thrust and libcu++. hipCCL installs libhipcxx under `<rocm>/include/hipccl`, which Bazel did not expose, so hipCUB could fail with 'libhipcxx could not be found'.

📝 Summary of Changes
This change works with both the legacy and the new (upcoming) hipccl layouts. It adds `:rocm_libhipcxx_includes`, which strips `include/hipccl` so the headers
are reachable by hipCUB, and depends on it from `:rocm_headers_includes`.

The glob covers the whole directory rather than naming subdirectories, because
libhipcxx headers cross-reference each other across cuda/, hip/, nv/ and
amd/. `allow_empty` leaves ROCm installs without `include/hipccl` unchanged.

🎯 Justification
This change is important to avoid build failures with ROCm's planned migration to hipCCL 3.x.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
N/A

🧪 Unit Tests:
Tested by building XLA in two ROCm containers:
- libhipcxx alone under include/hipccl, with hipCUB/rocPRIM/rocThrust in
include/
- the hipCCL layout, where hipCUB/rocPRIM/rocThrust are under include/hipccl too and include/{hipcub,rocprim,rocthrust} are symlinks into it

No unit tests were added.

🧪 Execution Tests:
N/A

Reviewed and approved for AMD by the ROCm XLA team in ROCm/xla#1419.
Copybara import of the project:

--
67fb5b65f46510c6f6e150ce2d3a605ac911a2cc by amd-mcieslak <323359018+amd-mcieslak@users.noreply.github.com>:

[ROCm] Expose libhipcxx from include/hipccl as its own include root

hipCCL3 installs libhipcxx under <rocm>/include/hipccl, which Bazel did not
expose, so hipCUB users failed with 'libhipcxx could not be found'. Works
with both the flat and the hipccl layout.

Merging this change closes #52725

display_title: Chunk sub-byte sub-tile packing in tiled linearizer.

head_commit.message:
Chunk sub-tile packing and unpacking in tiled linearizer

Linearizing sub-byte sub-tile-packed tensors and delinearizing sub-tile-packed tensors previously allocated an unpacked buffer spanning the entire array. Large sub-byte arrays caused tens of gigabytes of unreserved host memory growth.

This change transposes and repacks sub-byte host-to-device data and sub-tile-packed device-to-host data in bounded megabyte-scale chunks. Each chunk reuses small scratch storage and uses parallel transpose execution whenever the chunk plan exposes parallelism.

display_title: Support `register_with_cudart` in `embeddable_cuda_library` via `objcopy`

head_commit.message:
Support `register_with_cudart` in `embeddable_cuda_library` via `objcopy`

Replaces `-Wl,--wrap=__cudaRegister*` in `embeddable_cuda_library` and `cudart_kernel_registry` with an `objcopy --redefine-sym` rule (`_redefine_cuda_register_syms`) on the compiled object files, and adds a `register_with_cudart` attribute (defaulting to `True`).

When `register_with_cudart = True`, `__cudaRegisterFatBinary` and `__cudaRegisterFunction` are renamed to `__xla_cudart_cudaRegister*`, which registers the fatbinary and kernel symbols in XLA's `KernelRegistry` and forwards to `libcudart`.

When `register_with_cudart = False`, `__cudaRegisterFatBinary`, `__cudaRegisterFunction`, `__cudaRegisterFatBinaryEnd`, and `__cudaUnregisterFatBinary` are renamed to `__xla_isolated_cudaRegister*`, registering the fatbinary and kernel symbols only in XLA's `KernelRegistry` so `libcudart` never registers or eagerly loads the fatbinary.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Report group_sizes in CublasLtMatmulThunk::buffer_uses()

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Report group_sizes in CublasLtMatmulThunk::buffer_uses()

For grouped matmuls `CublasLtMatmulThunk::ExecuteOnStream` reads the
`group_sizes` buffer, but `buffer_uses()` did not list it. Command buffers rely
on `buffer_uses()` to determine which buffer allocations a recorded command
depends on, so a change of only the `group_sizes` device address between
executions went unnoticed and the previously recorded command could be replayed
with a stale address.

Report `group_sizes` as a read buffer use when it is present, so that command
buffer update tracking and the traced command buffer cache account for it.
Regular (non-grouped) matmuls are unaffected.

display_title: Reject negative mesh axis indices in AxisRef::Validate

head_commit.message:
Reject negative mesh axis indices in AxisRef::Validate

`AxisRef::Validate` only checked that the mesh axis index is less than the
number of mesh axes, so a negative index, e.g. one read from an `AxisRefProto`,
passed validation. `NamedSharding` and `MeshAxesReplicaGroupList` rely on this
validation in their constructors and afterwards use the index to look up mesh
axis sizes, which resulted in an out-of-bounds read.

`AxisRef::Validate` now also returns `InvalidArgument` for negative indices.
Both constructors already `CHECK` the validation result, so a negative index is
now rejected before it is used as an index.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject shardings with more last_tile_dims than tile assignment dimensions

`HloSharding::Subgroup` assumes that the number of subgroup types does not
exceed the rank of the tile assignment. Neither `HloSharding::FromProto` nor
the HLO text parser enforced this for `last_tile_dims`, so a malformed
`OpSharding` proto or sharding string made the computed number of data
dimensions negative and crashed the process.

Validate this where the sharding is deserialized: `HloSharding::FromProto` now
returns an error status and the HLO parser reports a parse error.

head_commit.message:
PR #52764: Bump lit from 23.1.4 to 23.1.5 Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52764 Bumps [lit](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project) from 23.1.4 to 23.1.5.
Release notes

Sourced from lit's releases.

LLVM 23.1.5 Release

  • Linux x86_64: xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • Linux Arm64: xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • macOS Apple Silicon (ARM64): xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • Windows x64 (64-bit): installer (signature), xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • Windows on Arm (ARM64): installer (signature), xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)

Download links for common platforms will appear above once builds have completed, if they are available. Check the full list of release packages at the bottom of this release page if you do not find a link above.

If you do not find a release package for your platform, you may be able to find a community built package on the LLVM Discourse forum thread for this release. Remember that these are built by volunteers and may not always be available. If you rely on a platform or configuration that is not one of the defaults, we suggest you use the binaries that your platform provides, or build your own release packages.

Package Types

Each platform has binary release packages. The file name starts with either LLVM- or clang+llvm- and ends with the platform's name. For example, LLVM-23.1.5-Linux-ARM64.tar.xz contains LLVM binaries for Arm64 Linux. Binary archive packages may be available as .tar.xz or .tar.zst files. The .tar.zst files contain the same package contents, but use zstd compression.

Except for Windows. Where LLVM-*.msi is an installer intended for using LLVM as a toolchain and the archive clang+llvm- contains the contents of the installer, plus libraries and tools not normally used in a toolchain. display_title: [XLA:GPU] Verify the reduction dimensions against the input in CudnnNormRewriter.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Verify the reduction dimensions against the input in CudnnNormRewriter.

When matching a layer norm pattern, the operand of the reduction that calculates
the expectation may differ from the layer norm input by a reshape or bitcast
that adds or removes degenerate dimensions. `MatchLayerNorm` nevertheless used
the dimensions of the reduction to index into the shape of the input when
deriving the transpose order and the shape of the cuDNN operands. If the
reduction's operand had a higher rank than the input, this resulted in
out-of-bounds accesses of the inverse transpose order and of the input's
dimensions.

The rewrite is now skipped unless all reduction dimensions are valid dimensions
of the input and select the same non-degenerate dimensions in the input as in
the reduction's operand. Patterns for which the dimensions agree are still
rewritten.

display_title: [XLA] Validate the reshape inferred_dimension when deserializing and parsing HLO

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Validate the reshape inferred_dimension when deserializing and parsing HLO

The `inferred_dimension` attribute of a `reshape` instruction was taken
verbatim from an `HloInstructionProto` or from HLO text. Dynamic dimension
inference later uses it to index into the dimensions of the result shape and
into a vector with one entry per result dimension, so a value that is not a
dimension of the result shape led to out-of-bounds accesses.

Reject such values where the instruction is created from external input:
`HloInstruction::CreateFromProto` now returns an error and the HLO parser
reports a parse error unless `inferred_dimension` is -1 (unset) or a valid
dimension index of the result shape. These are the two places where a reshape
is created with an `inferred_dimension` that comes from external input, so the
passes that consume the attribute do not need additional defensive checks.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019021506

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Report group_sizes in CublasLtMatmulThunk::buffer_uses()

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Report group_sizes in CublasLtMatmulThunk::buffer_uses()

For grouped matmuls `CublasLtMatmulThunk::ExecuteOnStream` reads the
`group_sizes` buffer, but `buffer_uses()` did not list it. Command buffers rely
on `buffer_uses()` to determine which buffer allocations a recorded command
depends on, so a change of only the `group_sizes` device address between
executions went unnoticed and the previously recorded command could be replayed
with a stale address.

Report `group_sizes` as a read buffer use when it is present, so that command
buffer update tracking and the traced command buffer cache account for it.
Regular (non-grouped) matmuls are unaffected.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019015197

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fix element count truncation when emitting large constants

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix element count truncation when emitting large constants

`ThunkEmitter::EmitConstant` stored the number of elements of a constant in an
`int`. For constants with 2^31 or more elements the count wrapped around, so
such a constant could be mistaken for a scalar: its global was sized as the
64 byte minimum allocation and `AppendGlobalConstant` copied the whole
content into the fixed 64 byte padding buffer, writing past its end.

Keep the element count as `int64_t`, so that only constants with at most one
element get an inline initializer, and only fill the padding buffer when the
content is actually smaller than the minimum allocation.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019017381

display_title: Compile CUDA command buffer kernels to CUBIN via embeddable_cuda_library

head_commit.message:
Compile CUDA command buffer kernels to CUBIN via embeddable_cuda_library

`command_buffer_kernels.cc` previously embedded `.target sm_50` PTX strings for `set_case_condition`, `set_while_condition`, and `noop`. On the first conditional command buffer recording per device, `CudaExecutor::LoadModuleFromPtx` JIT-compiled that PTX on the single-threaded `cuda_driver` pool, stalling first recording by ~187 ms on `sm_103a` and serializing compilation across GPUs.

So this change compiles `SetCaseCondition`, `SetWhileCondition`, and `NoOp` as CUDA C++ kernels in `command_buffer_kernels.cu.cc` using `embeddable_cuda_library` (with `register_with_cudart = False` so `libcudart` never registers or eagerly loads the fatbinary on drivers older than CUDA 12.3) and resolves their `KernelLoaderSpec`s via `FindCudaRuntimeKernel`. This returns in-memory CUBIN specs that `CudaExecutor::LoadKernel` loads directly via `LoadModuleFromCuBin` (`LoadCubin`), avoiding both the single-threaded PTX driver JIT and `cudaGetFuncBySymbol`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1018921780

PR #52763: Bump github/codeql-action/upload-sarif from 4.39.1 to 4.39.3 Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52763 Bumps [github/codeql-action/upload-sarif](https://github.com/github/codeql-action) from 4.39.1 to 4.39.3.
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/upload-sarif's releases.

v4.39.3

  • Fixed diff-informed alert filtering incorrectly removing alerts in changed files whose paths contain spaces, special characters, or non-ASCII characters. #4283

v4.39.2

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.4. #4284
  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.22.3 and earlier were discontinued on 16 October 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4266
  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode. If so, the CodeQL Action will emit a corresponding warning that will also be visible on the Tool Status Page. This check will be rolled out following this release of the CodeQL Action. #4221
  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. The analyze Action now warns if this environment variable is set. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243
Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/upload-sarif's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

No user facing changes.

  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode. If so, the CodeQL Action will emit a corresponding warning that will also be visible on the Tool Status Page. This check will be rolled out following this release of the CodeQL Action. #4221
  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. The analyze Action now warns if this environment variable is set. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243

4.39.1 - 21 Oct 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

4.39.0 - 15 Oct 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. 4.38.3 - 08 Oct 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.0. #4129

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Compile CUDA command buffer kernels to CUBIN via embeddable_cuda_library

head_commit.message:
Compile CUDA command buffer kernels to CUBIN via embeddable_cuda_library

`command_buffer_kernels.cc` previously embedded `.target sm_50` PTX strings for `set_case_condition`, `set_while_condition`, and `noop`. On the first conditional command buffer recording per device, `CudaExecutor::LoadModuleFromPtx` JIT-compiled that PTX on the single-threaded `cuda_driver` pool, stalling first recording by ~187 ms on `sm_103a` and serializing compilation across GPUs.

So this change compiles `SetCaseCondition`, `SetWhileCondition`, and `NoOp` as CUDA C++ kernels in `command_buffer_kernels.cu.cc` using `embeddable_cuda_library` (with `register_with_cudart = False` so `libcudart` never registers or eagerly loads the fatbinary on drivers older than CUDA 12.3) and resolves their `KernelLoaderSpec`s via `FindCudaRuntimeKernel`. This returns in-memory CUBIN specs that `CudaExecutor::LoadKernel` loads directly via `LoadModuleFromCuBin` (`LoadCubin`), avoiding both the single-threaded PTX driver JIT and `cudaGetFuncBySymbol`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1018921780

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Reject negative sort dimensions in the HLO verifier

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject negative sort dimensions in the HLO verifier

`ShapeVerifier::HandleSort` only checked that the sort dimension is smaller
than the operand rank. Because the comparison is signed, a negative sort
dimension in an HLO module (for example one deserialized from a proto or
parsed from HLO text) passed verification. Passes and backend code
generation that run afterwards index operand shapes with the sort dimension
without further checks, which leads to out-of-bounds accesses.

The verifier now also requires the sort dimension to be non-negative, so
such modules are rejected with an error before any pass consumes them.

The error message now reports the rank of the first operand instead of
reading the dimensions of the sort result shape, which is a tuple for
sorts with more than one operand and cannot be queried for dimensions.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019017541

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add tiling space and tile propagation for single-indexed gather

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add tiling space and tile propagation for single-indexed gather

`TilingSpace` now registers a runtime variable for the start index of a gather
with a single indexed dimension and no batching dimensions
(`TilingSpace::ProcessGather`), and `PropagateTileToInput` propagates a gather
output tile to its operands (`PropagateTileToInputForGatherOp`):
- `start_indices` gets the batch dimension tiles of the output (which must have
  size 1; their stride is normalized to 1) and a size-1 tile for
  `index_vector_dim`; this one-element tile defines the runtime variable.
- The gathered operand gets size-1 tiles on `collapsed_slice_dims`, the offset
  dimension tiles of the output on the other dimensions, and its indexed
  dimension is shifted by the runtime variable.
Unsupported gathers (several indexed dimensions, batching dimensions, sub-byte
types, unsigned index types, batch tiles larger than 1) return Unimplemented.

This is NFC for production: gather is still unsupported by the Triton support
checks, and every pass that tiles a fusion checks Triton support first (or only
sees fusions that are already Triton fusions); the CPU tiled emitter rejects
gather in `IsSupportedTiledFusion` before tiling.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013705685

head_commit.message:
PR #52764: Bump lit from 23.1.4 to 23.1.5 Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52764 Bumps [lit](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project) from 23.1.4 to 23.1.5.
Release notes

Sourced from lit's releases.

LLVM 23.1.5 Release

  • Linux x86_64: xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • Linux Arm64: xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • macOS Apple Silicon (ARM64): xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • Windows x64 (64-bit): installer (signature), xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • Windows on Arm (ARM64): installer (signature), xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)

Download links for common platforms will appear above once builds have completed, if they are available. Check the full list of release packages at the bottom of this release page if you do not find a link above.

If you do not find a release package for your platform, you may be able to find a community built package on the LLVM Discourse forum thread for this release. Remember that these are built by volunteers and may not always be available. If you rely on a platform or configuration that is not one of the defaults, we suggest you use the binaries that your platform provides, or build your own release packages.

Package Types

Each platform has binary release packages. The file name starts with either LLVM- or clang+llvm- and ends with the platform's name. For example, LLVM-23.1.5-Linux-ARM64.tar.xz contains LLVM binaries for Arm64 Linux. Binary archive packages may be available as .tar.xz or .tar.zst files. The .tar.zst files contain the same package contents, but use zstd compression.

Except for Windows. Where LLVM-*.msi is an installer intended for using LLVM as a toolchain and the archive clang+llvm- contains the contents of the installer, plus libraries and tools not normally used in a toolchain. You most likely want the LLVM- installer, unless you are developing software which itself uses LLVM, in which case choose clang+llvm-.

In addition, source archives are available:

  • To get all the llvm-project source code for this release, choose llvm-project-23.1.5.src.tar.xz.
  • test-suite-23.1.5.src.tar.xz is an archive of the LLVM Test Suite) for this release.

Verifying Packages

All packages come with a matching .sig and/or .jsonl file. You should use these to verify the integrity of the packages.

If it has a .sig file, it should have been signed by the release managers using GPG. Download the keys from the LLVM website, import them into your keyring and use them to verify the file:

$ gpg --import release-keys.asc
$ gpg --verify <package file name>.sig <package file name>

If it has a .jsonl file, use gh to verify the package:

$ gh attestation verify --repo llvm/llvm-project <package file name>
(if you are able to connect to GitHub)
$ gh attestation verify --repo llvm/llvm-project <package file name> --bundle <package file name>.jsonl
(using attestation file on disk)

display_title: Validate original value shape indices when deserializing HLO instructions

head_commit.message:
Validate original value shape indices when deserializing HLO instructions

`HloInstruction::CreateFromProto` passed the shape indices of an
`OriginalValueProto` to `OriginalValue::FromProto` without checking them
against the shape of the instruction. The tuple tree built from these indices
grows with the magnitude and the length of the indices, so a small malformed
proto could cause excessive memory allocation or very deep recursion before
the HLO verifier had a chance to run.

`HloInstruction::CreateFromProto` now returns an `InvalidArgument` error if an
element of the original value has a shape index that does not exist in the
shape of the instruction, which bounds the size of the tree by the size of the
shape. The HLO verifier already rejects original values whose tuple structure
differs from the instruction shape, so modules that pass verification are not
affected.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019017201

display_title: Support `register_with_cudart` in `embeddable_cuda_library` via `objcopy`

head_commit.message:
Support `register_with_cudart` in `embeddable_cuda_library` via `objcopy`

Replaces `-Wl,--wrap=__cudaRegister*` in `embeddable_cuda_library` and `cudart_kernel_registry` with an `objcopy --redefine-sym` rule (`_redefine_cuda_register_syms`) on the compiled object files, and adds a `register_with_cudart` attribute (defaulting to `True`).

When `register_with_cudart = True`, `__cudaRegisterFatBinary` and `__cudaRegisterFunction` are renamed to `__xla_cudart_cudaRegister*`, which registers the fatbinary and kernel symbols in XLA's `KernelRegistry` and forwards to `libcudart`.

When `register_with_cudart = False`, `__cudaRegisterFatBinary`, `__cudaRegisterFunction`, `__cudaRegisterFatBinaryEnd`, and `__cudaUnregisterFatBinary` are renamed to `__xla_isolated_cudaRegister*`, registering the fatbinary and kernel symbols only in XLA's `KernelRegistry` so `libcudart` never registers or eagerly loads the fatbinary.

head_commit.message:
PR #52764: Bump lit from 23.1.4 to 23.1.5 Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52764 Bumps [lit](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project) from 23.1.4 to 23.1.5.
Release notes

Sourced from lit's releases.

LLVM 23.1.5 Release

  • Linux x86_64: xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • Linux Arm64: xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • macOS Apple Silicon (ARM64): xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • Windows x64 (64-bit): installer (signature), xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • Windows on Arm (ARM64): installer (signature), xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)

Download links for common platforms will appear above once builds have completed, if they are available. Check the full list of release packages at the bottom of this release page if you do not find a link above.

If you do not find a release package for your platform, you may be able to find a community built package on the LLVM Discourse forum thread for this release. Remember that these are built by volunteers and may not always be available. If you rely on a platform or configuration that is not one of the defaults, we suggest you use the binaries that your platform provides, or build your own release packages.

Package Types

Each platform has binary release packages. The file name starts with either LLVM- or clang+llvm- and ends with the platform's name. For example, LLVM-23.1.5-Linux-ARM64.tar.xz contains LLVM binaries for Arm64 Linux. Binary archive packages may be available as .tar.xz or .tar.zst files. The .tar.zst files contain the same package contents, but use zstd compression.

Except for Windows. Where LLVM-*.msi is an installer intended for using LLVM as a toolchain and the archive clang+llvm- contains the contents of the installer, plus libraries and tools not normally used in a toolchain. You most likely want the LLVM- installer, unless you are developing software which itself uses LLVM, in which case choose clang+llvm-.

In addition, source archives are available:

  • To get all the llvm-project source code for this release, choose llvm-project-23.1.5.src.tar.xz.
  • test-suite-23.1.5.src.tar.xz is an archive of the LLVM Test Suite) for this release.

Verifying Packages

All packages come with a matching .sig and/or .jsonl file. You should use these to verify the integrity of the packages.

If it has a .sig file, it should have been signed by the release managers using GPG. Download the keys from the LLVM website, import them into your keyring and use them to verify the file:

$ gpg --import release-keys.asc
$ gpg --verify <package file name>.sig <package file name>

If it has a .jsonl file, use gh to verify the package:

$ gh attestation verify --repo llvm/llvm-project <package file name>
(if you are able to connect to GitHub)
$ gh attestation verify --repo llvm/llvm-project <package file name> --bundle <package file name>.jsonl
(using attestation file on disk)

display_title: [XLA] Don't simplify a mixed precision reduce to a reshape

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Don't simplify a mixed precision reduce to a reshape

`AlgebraicSimplifier` replaces a reduce that keeps the number of elements with
a reshape of its input. For a mixed precision reduce, whose result element type
differs from the element type of its input (e.g. an `f16` input reduced into an
`f32` result), this created a reshape whose shape has a different element type
than its operand. Such a reshape is invalid, and later passes that rely on the
declared shape, such as constant folding, could then read the operand data
using the wrong element type.

Only apply the rewrite if every result of the reduce has the same element type
as the corresponding input. Mixed precision reduces are left unchanged.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019017789

display_title: [IFRT IR] Null-terminate text atom programs before deserialization

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Null-terminate text atom programs before deserialization

`IfrtAtomProgramsFromVhloPass` passed a flattened `absl::Cord`, which is not null-terminated, to the MLIR parser. Atom programs are normally MLIR bytecode, but text input is parsed by the MLIR lexer, which assumes a null-terminated buffer and could read past the end of the atom program.

Copy the atom program to a `std::string` when it is not MLIR bytecode. Bytecode is still deserialized without a copy.

display_title: [XLA] Check operand element types of elementwise ops in HloEvaluator

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Check operand element types of elementwise ops in HloEvaluator

`HloEvaluator` evaluates elementwise unary, binary and ternary operations, and
`rng`, by reading the values of their operands as a fixed element type, in most
cases the element type of the result. Nothing checked that the evaluated
operands actually have that element type. This is not guaranteed: the operands
of a mixed precision instruction can differ in floating point precision from
each other and from the result, and some data movement operations (e.g.
reshape) evaluate to the element type of their operand rather than their own.
The operand was then read as the wrong element type, which reads past the end
of its buffer if the actual element type is narrower.

Check the element types of the evaluated operands, once per instruction, in the
shared elementwise helpers and in `HandleRng`, and return an error on a
mismatch. Evaluating such an instruction now fails, so for example constant
folding leaves it in place, instead of computing a result from misinterpreted
data.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019058316

display_title: [XLA] Bounds-check table lookup indices in collective_opt_utils

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Bounds-check table lookup indices in collective_opt_utils

The collective pattern matchers evaluate table lookups, i.e. a dynamic-slice
of a rank-1 constant indexed by a device id or by another table lookup, at
compile time. The index was only checked for being non-negative before it was
used to read the constant's literal, and the literal accessors only validate
indices with `DCHECK`. A module whose replica groups or tables yield an index
past the end of a table therefore caused an out-of-bounds read in optimized
builds.

Route all four table reads (`GetIndexForId`, `IsPerIdOffsets`,
`EvaluateOffset` and `GetIndicesSpecForDynamicSlice`) through a single
`GetTableEntry` helper that returns `nullopt` when the index is outside the
constant table, so that the pattern simply does not match. Lookups into iota
tables are unchanged since they do not read a literal.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019018870

display_title: [XLA] Validate the reshape inferred_dimension when deserializing and parsing HLO

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Validate the reshape inferred_dimension when deserializing and parsing HLO

The `inferred_dimension` attribute of a `reshape` instruction was taken
verbatim from an `HloInstructionProto` or from HLO text. Dynamic dimension
inference later uses it to index into the dimensions of the result shape and
into a vector with one entry per result dimension, so a value that is not a
dimension of the result shape led to out-of-bounds accesses.

Reject such values where the instruction is created from external input:
`HloInstruction::CreateFromProto` now returns an error and the HLO parser
reports a parse error unless `inferred_dimension` is -1 (unset) or a valid
dimension index of the result shape. These are the two places where a reshape
is created with an `inferred_dimension` that comes from external input, so the
passes that consume the attribute do not need additional defensive checks.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019021506

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Verify the reduction dimensions against the input in CudnnNormRewriter.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Verify the reduction dimensions against the input in CudnnNormRewriter.

When matching a layer norm pattern, the operand of the reduction that calculates
the expectation may differ from the layer norm input by a reshape or bitcast
that adds or removes degenerate dimensions. `MatchLayerNorm` nevertheless used
the dimensions of the reduction to index into the shape of the input when
deriving the transpose order and the shape of the cuDNN operands. If the
reduction's operand had a higher rank than the input, this resulted in
out-of-bounds accesses of the inverse transpose order and of the input's
dimensions.

The rewrite is now skipped unless all reduction dimensions are valid dimensions
of the input and select the same non-degenerate dimensions in the input as in
the reduction's operand. Patterns for which the dimensions agree are still
rewritten.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Report group_sizes in CublasLtMatmulThunk::buffer_uses()

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Report group_sizes in CublasLtMatmulThunk::buffer_uses()

For grouped matmuls `CublasLtMatmulThunk::ExecuteOnStream` reads the
`group_sizes` buffer, but `buffer_uses()` did not list it. Command buffers rely
on `buffer_uses()` to determine which buffer allocations a recorded command
depends on, so a change of only the `group_sizes` device address between
executions went unnoticed and the previously recorded command could be replayed
with a stale address.

Report `group_sizes` as a read buffer use when it is present, so that command
buffer update tracking and the traced command buffer cache account for it.
Regular (non-grouped) matmuls are unaffected.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019015197

display_title: [IFRT Proxy] Validate array specs of client-supplied RemapPlans on the server.

head_commit.message:
[IFRT Proxy] Validate array specs of client-supplied RemapPlans on the server.

`IfrtBackend::HandleRemapArraysRequest` deserialized the `RemapPlan` sent by
the proxy client and passed it to `Client::RemapArrays()` without validating
it. Whether an inconsistent plan was rejected therefore depended on the IFRT
implementation behind the server, and not all of them check it. PjRt-IFRT, for
example, does not compare the input and output array specs of a plan, so a
plan whose output dtype or shape disagrees with its inputs produced arrays
whose metadata does not describe their buffers.

The server now calls `RemapPlan::ValidateArraySpecs()` right after
deserializing the plan and returns the error to the client. This checks the
array indices used by the plan and that mapped input and output arrays agree
on dtype, shard shape, memory kind and layout. It is the lightweight
validation that `RemapPlan` asks `Client::RemapArrays()` implementations to
perform at least, and its result is cached in the plan, so implementations
that validate again do not repeat the work. The slower shard-level checks of
`RemapPlan::Validate()` are not run per request and remain the responsibility
of the implementation.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019020697

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fix element count truncation when emitting large constants

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix element count truncation when emitting large constants

`ThunkEmitter::EmitConstant` stored the number of elements of a constant in an
`int`. For constants with 2^31 or more elements the count wrapped around, so
such a constant could be mistaken for a scalar: its global was sized as the
64 byte minimum allocation and `AppendGlobalConstant` copied the whole
content into the fixed 64 byte padding buffer, writing past its end.

Keep the element count as `int64_t`, so that only constants with at most one
element get an inline initializer, and only fill the padding buffer when the
content is actually smaller than the minimum allocation.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019017381

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Check operand element types of elementwise ops in HloEvaluator

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Check operand element types of elementwise ops in HloEvaluator

`HloEvaluator` evaluates elementwise unary, binary and ternary operations, and
`rng`, by reading the values of their operands as a fixed element type, in most
cases the element type of the result. Nothing checked that the evaluated
operands actually have that element type. This is not guaranteed: the operands
of a mixed precision instruction can differ in floating point precision from
each other and from the result, and some data movement operations (e.g.
reshape) evaluate to the element type of their operand rather than their own.
The operand was then read as the wrong element type, which reads past the end
of its buffer if the actual element type is narrower.

Check the element types of the evaluated operands, once per instruction, in the
shared elementwise helpers and in `HandleRng`, and return an error on a
mismatch. Evaluating such an instruction now fails, so for example constant
folding leaves it in place, instead of computing a result from misinterpreted
data.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019058316

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Don't simplify a mixed precision reduce to a reshape

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Don't simplify a mixed precision reduce to a reshape

`AlgebraicSimplifier` replaces a reduce that keeps the number of elements with
a reshape of its input. For a mixed precision reduce, whose result element type
differs from the element type of its input (e.g. an `f16` input reduced into an
`f32` result), this created a reshape whose shape has a different element type
than its operand. Such a reshape is invalid, and later passes that rely on the
declared shape, such as constant folding, could then read the operand data
using the wrong element type.

Only apply the rewrite if every result of the reduce has the same element type
as the corresponding input. Mixed precision reduces are left unchanged.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019017789

display_title: Reject negative mesh axis indices in AxisRef::Validate

head_commit.message:
Reject negative mesh axis indices in AxisRef::Validate

`AxisRef::Validate` only checked that the mesh axis index is less than the
number of mesh axes, so a negative index, e.g. one read from an `AxisRefProto`,
passed validation. `NamedSharding` and `MeshAxesReplicaGroupList` rely on this
validation in their constructors and afterwards use the index to look up mesh
axis sizes, which resulted in an out-of-bounds read.

`AxisRef::Validate` now also returns `InvalidArgument` for negative indices.
Both constructors already `CHECK` the validation result, so a negative index is
now rejected before it is used as an index.

display_title: [XLA] Validate in-place collective-permute protos during deserialization

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Validate in-place collective-permute protos during deserialization

`HloInstruction::CreateFromProto` regroups the flat `dynamic_slice_sizes` of an
in-place `collective-permute` or `collective-permute-start` into one list per
slice, based on the shapes of the input and start-indices operands. Those
operands and shapes come from the proto and have not been verified at that
point, yet they were used without validation. A proto with fewer than four
operands, with start indices that are not (nested) non-empty tuples, or with
fewer slice sizes than the shapes imply caused out-of-bounds reads, and start
indices describing more slices for a later buffer than for the first one caused
an out-of-bounds write. The existing `CHECK_GE` bound on `dynamic_slice_sizes`
was also off by one.

Return an error for such protos instead: require exactly four operands, check
the operand shapes before indexing into them, and bounds-check every read of
`dynamic_slice_sizes` and every write to the list of slices.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019018379

display_title: [XLA] Reject shardings with more last_tile_dims than tile assignment dimensions

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject shardings with more last_tile_dims than tile assignment dimensions

`HloSharding::Subgroup` assumes that the number of subgroup types does not
exceed the rank of the tile assignment. Neither `HloSharding::FromProto` nor
the HLO text parser enforced this for `last_tile_dims`, so a malformed
`OpSharding` proto or sharding string made the computed number of data
dimensions negative and crashed the process.

Validate this where the sharding is deserialized: `HloSharding::FromProto` now
returns an error status and the HLO parser reports a parse error.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Bounds-check table lookup indices in collective_opt_utils

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Bounds-check table lookup indices in collective_opt_utils

The collective pattern matchers evaluate table lookups, i.e. a dynamic-slice
of a rank-1 constant indexed by a device id or by another table lookup, at
compile time. The index was only checked for being non-negative before it was
used to read the constant's literal, and the literal accessors only validate
indices with `DCHECK`. A module whose replica groups or tables yield an index
past the end of a table therefore caused an out-of-bounds read in optimized
builds.

Route all four table reads (`GetIndexForId`, `IsPerIdOffsets`,
`EvaluateOffset` and `GetIndicesSpecForDynamicSlice`) through a single
`GetTableEntry` helper that returns `nullopt` when the index is outside the
constant table, so that the pattern simply does not match. Lookups into iota
tables are unchanged since they do not read a literal.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019018870

display_title: [XLA:LHS] Fix out-of-bounds access when no annotated node can be scheduled

head_commit.message:
[XLA:LHS] Fix out-of-bounds access when no annotated node can be scheduled

`FindAndExtractBestAnnotatedNode` removed the chosen node from the annotation
ready set by swapping it with the last element, without checking that a node
had been chosen. When every ready node of the annotation group crosses the
resource overlap limit, the iterator still points past the end of the vector,
so the swap read and wrote one element out of bounds before the caller reported
the failure.

Return early in that case and leave the ready set untouched. The caller already
turns the missing node into an error status, so scheduling such a module now
fails cleanly instead of corrupting memory.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019019929

head_commit.message:
PR #52764: Bump lit from 23.1.4 to 23.1.5 Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52764 Bumps [lit](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project) from 23.1.4 to 23.1.5.
Release notes

Sourced from lit's releases.

LLVM 23.1.5 Release

  • Linux x86_64: xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • Linux Arm64: xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • macOS Apple Silicon (ARM64): xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • Windows x64 (64-bit): installer (signature), xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)
  • Windows on Arm (ARM64): installer (signature), xz archive (signature), zstd archive (signature)

Download links for common platforms will appear above once builds have completed, if they are available. Check the full list of release packages at the bottom of this release page if you do not find a link above.

If you do not find a release package for your platform, you may be able to find a community built package on the LLVM Discourse forum thread for this release. Remember that these are built by volunteers and may not always be available. If you rely on a platform or configuration that is not one of the defaults, we suggest you use the binaries that your platform provides, or build your own release packages.

Package Types

Each platform has binary release packages. The file name starts with either LLVM- or clang+llvm- and ends with the platform's name. For example, LLVM-23.1.5-Linux-ARM64.tar.xz contains LLVM binaries for Arm64 Linux. Binary archive packages may be available as .tar.xz or .tar.zst files. The .tar.zst files contain the same package contents, but use zstd compression.

Except for Windows. Where LLVM-*.msi is an installer intended for using LLVM as a toolchain and the archive clang+llvm- contains the contents of the installer, plus libraries and tools not normally used in a toolchain. You most likely want the LLVM- installer, unless you are developing software which itself uses LLVM, in which case choose clang+llvm-.

In addition, source archives are available:

  • To get all the llvm-project source code for this release, choose llvm-project-23.1.5.src.tar.xz.
  • test-suite-23.1.5.src.tar.xz is an archive of the LLVM Test Suite) for this release.

Verifying Packages

All packages come with a matching .sig and/or .jsonl file. You should use these to verify the integrity of the packages.

If it has a .sig file, it should have been signed by the release managers using GPG. Download the keys from the LLVM website, import them into your keyring and use them to verify the file:

$ gpg --import release-keys.asc

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Reject negative sort dimensions in the HLO verifier

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject negative sort dimensions in the HLO verifier

`ShapeVerifier::HandleSort` only checked that the sort dimension is smaller
than the operand rank. Because the comparison is signed, a negative sort
dimension in an HLO module (for example one deserialized from a proto or
parsed from HLO text) passed verification. Passes and backend code
generation that run afterwards index operand shapes with the sort dimension
without further checks, which leads to out-of-bounds accesses.

The verifier now also requires the sort dimension to be non-negative, so
such modules are rejected with an error before any pass consumes them.

The error message now reports the rank of the first operand instead of
reading the dimensions of the sort result shape, which is a tuple for
sorts with more than one operand and cannot be queried for dimensions.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019017541

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [PjRt-IFRT] Return an error for duplicate shards in `HloShardingSpec::IndexDomains`

head_commit.message:
[PjRt-IFRT] Return an error for duplicate shards in `HloShardingSpec::IndexDomains`

The fast path of `HloShardingSpec::IndexDomains` stores one `IndexDomain` per
tile into a per-shard `std::optional` slot and then dereferences every slot
unconditionally. This assumes that the tile assignment of the wrapped
`xla::HloSharding` contains every shard exactly once, but nothing enforces it:
`xla::HloSharding::FromProto` accepts a tile assignment that repeats a device.
With such a sharding, e.g. one deserialized from a malformed proto, a slot stays
empty and reading it is undefined behavior.

Check that every slot has been filled and return an `InvalidArgumentError`
otherwise. `HloShardingSpec::Disassemble` uses `IndexDomains` for shapes that
are not evenly divisible and now returns the same error.

The check lives in `IndexDomains` because an `HloShardingSpec` can be created
from several independent sources (sharding and sharding spec deserialization,
executable metadata deserialization, and direct construction) that all end in
`HloShardingSpec::Create`, which cannot report an error. It costs one branch per
shard on a path that already constructs an `IndexDomain` per shard.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019019394

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Validate original value shape indices when deserializing HLO instructions

head_commit.message:
Validate original value shape indices when deserializing HLO instructions

`HloInstruction::CreateFromProto` passed the shape indices of an
`OriginalValueProto` to `OriginalValue::FromProto` without checking them
against the shape of the instruction. The tuple tree built from these indices
grows with the magnitude and the length of the indices, so a small malformed
proto could cause excessive memory allocation or very deep recursion before
the HLO verifier had a chance to run.

`HloInstruction::CreateFromProto` now returns an `InvalidArgument` error if an
element of the original value has a shape index that does not exist in the
shape of the instruction, which bounds the size of the tree by the size of the
shape. The HLO verifier already rejects original values whose tuple structure
differs from the instruction shape, so modules that pass verification are not
affected.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019017201

display_title: PR #52725: [XLA:GPU] Expose ROCm's libhipcxx from include/hipccl as its own include root

head_commit.message:
PR #52725: [XLA:GPU] Expose ROCm's libhipcxx from include/hipccl as its own include root

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52725

Motivation
As part of the move to the CCCL 3.0-3.3 API, AMD is introducing hipCCL, a
unified package for rocPRIM, hipCUB and rocThrust that mirrors the role
NVIDIA's CCCL plays for CUB, Thrust and libcu++. hipCCL installs libhipcxx under `<rocm>/include/hipccl`, which Bazel did not expose, so hipCUB could fail with 'libhipcxx could not be found'.

📝 Summary of Changes
This change works with both the legacy and the new (upcoming) hipccl layouts. It adds `:rocm_libhipcxx_includes`, which strips `include/hipccl` so the headers
are reachable by hipCUB, and depends on it from `:rocm_headers_includes`.

The glob covers the whole directory rather than naming subdirectories, because
libhipcxx headers cross-reference each other across cuda/, hip/, nv/ and
amd/. `allow_empty` leaves ROCm installs without `include/hipccl` unchanged.

🎯 Justification
This change is important to avoid build failures with ROCm's planned migration to hipCCL 3.x.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
N/A

🧪 Unit Tests:
Tested by building XLA in two ROCm containers:
- libhipcxx alone under include/hipccl, with hipCUB/rocPRIM/rocThrust in
include/
- the hipCCL layout, where hipCUB/rocPRIM/rocThrust are under include/hipccl too and include/{hipcub,rocprim,rocthrust} are symlinks into it

No unit tests were added.

🧪 Execution Tests:
N/A

Reviewed and approved for AMD by the ROCm XLA team in ROCm/xla#1419.

display_title: [XLA:TSL] Reject negative byte counts in SnappyInputBuffer

head_commit.message:
[XLA:TSL] Reject negative byte counts in SnappyInputBuffer

SnappyInputBuffer::ReadNBytes passed a negative bytes_to_read to
tstring::resize_uninitialized, which takes a size_t. A count of -1 hit
the __builtin_trap in TF_TString_ResizeUninitialized and killed the
process; other negative counts convert to a size of 2^63 or more.
BufferedInputStream and RandomAccessInputStream return InvalidArgument
for a negative count.

Return InvalidArgument from SnappyInputBuffer::ReadNBytes the same way,
before result is touched. Add a test that a negative count is rejected,
in a new snappy_inputbuffer_test target so that snappy_test.cc is not
modified.

Companion to the SnappyInputStream change in #52698; see the discussion
in #52502.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Vectorize small kLoop phases on Hopper and newer GPUs.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Vectorize small kLoop phases on Hopper and newer GPUs.

`ComputeLoopFusionConfig` disables loop unrolling and vectorization when the output element count is smaller than the total hardware thread capacity (`threads_per_core_limit * core_count`), forcing `unroll_factor = 1` for every small stage considered by `MultiPhaseFusion` and phased nodes in `ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion`. Inside phased fusions, leaving small `kLoop` stages unvectorized inflates block counts past the 8-block cluster limit or forces multi-block cluster barriers where vectorized threads would fit into a single block.

Allow `ComputeLoopFusionConfig`, `LoopFusion`, and `ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion::CreateNativeNestedEmitter` to opt into unrolling small fusions via `unroll_small_inputs` / `unroll_small_fusions`, and enable it on Hopper and newer CUDA GPUs (`IsAtLeastHopper()`) in `MultiPhaseFusion` and for `kLoop` leaves inside phased nodes of `ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1017304379

  `--xla_dump_isolated_hlos_pre_and_post_config_assignment`
- `--xla_gpu_dump_autotune_logs_to` → `--xla_dump_autotune_logs_to`
- `--xla_gpu_override_gemm_autotuner` → `--xla_gpu_override_triton_config`
- `--xla_gpu_gemm_autotuner_override_file` →
  `--xla_gpu_override_triton_configs_file`

Add the new fields to `DebugOptions`, remove and reserve the old proto fields in
`xla.proto`, and keep the deprecated CLI flags as aliases that populate the new

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Handle root GemmFusion outputs like any other output.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Handle root GemmFusion outputs like any other output.

GemmFusion special-cased a fusion output that is the root of its computation: it set the new root by hand and removed the old instruction instead of calling `ReplaceInstruction`. Every other output goes through `ReplaceInstruction`, which also carries the replaced instruction's frontend attributes, metadata and control dependencies over to the replacement. The fusion, or the bitcast that replaces the output, therefore inherited those only when the replaced instruction was not the root.

`ReplaceInstruction` already updates the computation root, so the special case is not needed. Remove it so that root and non-root outputs are replaced the same way.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Handle root GemmFusion outputs like any other output.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Handle root GemmFusion outputs like any other output.

GemmFusion special-cased a fusion output that is the root of its computation: it set the new root by hand and removed the old instruction instead of calling `ReplaceInstruction`. Every other output goes through `ReplaceInstruction`, which also carries the replaced instruction's frontend attributes, metadata and control dependencies over to the replacement. The fusion, or the bitcast that replaces the output, therefore inherited those only when the replaced instruction was not the root.

`ReplaceInstruction` already updates the computation root, so the special case is not needed. Remove it so that root and non-root outputs are replaced the same way.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Drop removed instructions from the HloCSE representative set

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Drop removed instructions from the HloCSE representative set

HloCSE can remove an instruction that it has already recorded as the
representative of its equivalence class: a duplicate iota operand of the
instruction being visited, or an operand that becomes unused when a duplicate
instruction is replaced. The removed instruction stayed in the set, so an
equivalent instruction visited later was replaced with it. That left live
instructions with an operand that is no longer part of the computation and
that is deleted when the module is cleaned up.

Erase such instructions from the set before they are removed. The extra
lookup only happens for instructions that HloCSE removes in addition to the
duplicate it is replacing, so the common path is unchanged.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Guard RawBufferEntry and PjRtBufferEntry state against concurrent Handle calls.

head_commit.message:
Guard RawBufferEntry and PjRtBufferEntry state against concurrent Handle calls.

`PullTable::Handle` releases the table lock before calling `Entry::Handle`, and
`AwaitPull` replays paused pulls on the registering thread after the entry has
been published. A pull that arrives on the event loop thread at that moment runs
`Entry::Handle` concurrently on the same entry. `RawBufferEntry` and
`PjRtBufferEntry` moved the buffer out of their per-buffer state and updated
`num_consumed_bufs_` without synchronization (`mu_` was declared but never
acquired), so two threads could both take ownership of the same buffer
reference, corrupting its reference count and leading to a use-after-free.

Both entries now take the buffer out of `arrs_` and update `num_consumed_bufs_`
while holding `mu_`. The lock is not held while the readiness callback is
registered, since that callback may schedule the copy and send inline. The
thread-safety requirement is documented on `PullTable::Entry::Handle`, and a
regression test races two `Handle` calls on the same buffer for both entry
types.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019018609

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Compile CUDA command buffer kernels to CUBIN via embeddable_cuda_library

head_commit.message:
Compile CUDA command buffer kernels to CUBIN via embeddable_cuda_library

`command_buffer_kernels.cc` previously embedded `.target sm_50` PTX strings for `set_case_condition`, `set_while_condition`, and `noop`. On the first conditional command buffer recording per device, `CudaExecutor::LoadModuleFromPtx` JIT-compiled that PTX on the single-threaded `cuda_driver` pool, stalling first recording by ~187 ms on `sm_103a` and serializing compilation across GPUs.

So this change compiles `SetCaseCondition`, `SetWhileCondition`, and `NoOp` as CUDA C++ kernels in `command_buffer_kernels.cu.cc` using `embeddable_cuda_library` (with `register_with_cudart = False` so `libcudart` never registers or eagerly loads the fatbinary on drivers older than CUDA 12.3) and resolves their `KernelLoaderSpec`s via `FindCudaRuntimeKernel`. This returns in-memory CUBIN specs that `CudaExecutor::LoadKernel` loads directly via `LoadModuleFromCuBin` (`LoadCubin`), avoiding both the single-threaded PTX driver JIT and `cudaGetFuncBySymbol`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1018921780

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Bound the traversal of MLIR locations when exporting them to HLO metadata.

head_commit.message:
Bound the traversal of MLIR locations when exporting them to HLO metadata.

MLIR uniques locations, so nested locations (`CallSiteLoc`, `FusedLoc`,
`NameLoc`) can share sub-locations and form a DAG. The MHLO to HLO export
walked such locations as trees when building op names, stack frames and source
file/line metadata. With shared sub-locations, the work and the size of the
exported metadata grew exponentially with the nesting depth, far beyond the
size of the module.

Each of these traversals now visits at most 4096 locations per exported
location and ignores the rest. Locations emitted by frontends are far smaller,
so their metadata is unchanged; only pathologically nested locations get
truncated metadata.

Shared sub-locations are still visited every time they occur instead of being
deduplicated, because repeated locations are legitimate, for example the stack
frames of a recursive function.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019021072

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Synchronize single-block phases via block barriers.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Synchronize single-block phases via block barriers.

Phased nodes in `ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion` previously emitted a cluster barrier at every phase boundary and configured even pure single-block fusions as 1-block thread-block clusters. When consecutive phases each execute on a single block (`bid == 0`), cluster barriers pay unnecessary GPC barrier latency and flush SM L1 cache lines that would otherwise stay hot across phases.

Group contiguous runs of single-block phases under a shared `bid < 1` guard and synchronize transitions between single-block phases with a block barrier outside any thread-count guard. When every phase in a phased node uses a single block, omit cluster launch dimensions so pure single-block fusions launch without a thread-block cluster.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1017280619

display_title: Support `register_with_cudart` in `embeddable_cuda_library` via `objcopy`

head_commit.message:
Support `register_with_cudart` in `embeddable_cuda_library` via `objcopy`

Replaces `-Wl,--wrap=__cudaRegister*` in `embeddable_cuda_library` and `cudart_kernel_registry` with an `objcopy --redefine-sym` rule (`_redefine_cuda_register_syms`) on the compiled object files, and adds a `register_with_cudart` attribute (defaulting to `True`).

When `register_with_cudart = True`, `__cudaRegisterFatBinary` and `__cudaRegisterFunction` are renamed to `__xla_cudart_cudaRegister*`, which registers the fatbinary and kernel symbols in XLA's `KernelRegistry` and forwards to `libcudart`.

When `register_with_cudart = False`, `__cudaRegisterFatBinary`, `__cudaRegisterFunction`, `__cudaRegisterFatBinaryEnd`, and `__cudaUnregisterFatBinary` are renamed to `__xla_isolated_cudaRegister*`, registering the fatbinary and kernel symbols only in XLA's `KernelRegistry` so `libcudart` never registers or eagerly loads the fatbinary.

display_title: [XLA] Don't annotate integer abs as non-negative if the input may be INT_MIN

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Don't annotate integer abs as non-negative if the input may be INT_MIN

`SimplifyArithPass` annotated the result of the integer abs pattern
`select(x >= 0, x, 0 - x)` with the range `[0, INT_MAX]` even if nothing was
known about `x`. This does not hold for the minimum signed value, for which
`0 - x` wraps around to `x` itself, so the result is negative. The unsound
range could then be used to drop a lower-bound clamp on an index computed from
such a value.

Only annotate the result if the range of `x` is known and excludes the minimum
signed value of its type. The annotation for inputs whose known range excludes
that value is unchanged.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019017906

display_title: [XLA] Remove unnecessary `CallContext::kControlFlow` checks in `HloLivenessAnalysis`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Remove unnecessary `CallContext::kControlFlow` checks in `HloLivenessAnalysis`.

`PropagateLivenessToParameterCallers` and `PropagateLivenessThroughControlFlow`
already check each caller instruction's opcode (`kWhile`, `kCall`,
`kConditional`), so gating them on
`call_graph_node.context() == CallContext::kControlFlow` had no reason to be
there. Worse, when a `while`, `call`, or `conditional` is nested inside an
embedded computation such as `map`, `CallGraph` marks its callee computations
`CallContext::kEmbedded` (or `kBoth` if shared), so the check suppressed
liveness propagation to the caller and let `HloModuleDCE` treat live
loop-carried tuple elements as dead.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [CHLO] Do not recompose composites with a mismatched region count

head_commit.message:
[CHLO] Do not recompose composites with a mismatched region count

`ChloOpRecomposePattern` moves the regions of a `stablehlo.composite` into the
CHLO op it creates by zipping both region lists with `llvm::zip_equal`.
`stablehlo.composite` accepts any number of regions, while the CHLO ops have a
fixed number, and nothing checked that the two agree. `zip_equal` only asserts
on equal lengths; without assertions it iterates over the composite's regions,
so a composite with more regions than the CHLO op made the pattern access
regions past the end of the new op, and one with fewer left the new op with an
empty region.

Compare the region counts before moving the regions and fail the match when
they differ, erasing the op that was just created so the IR is left unchanged.
Such a composite is then left in place, like any other composite that the
pass does not recompose.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019015280

display_title: Fix spatial-minor backward weight conv rewrite on v6e+

head_commit.message:
Fix spatial-minor backward weight conv rewrite on v6e+

When `SpaceToBatchConverter` propagates a space-to-batch split into a backward-weight (`window_dilation`) convolution, it folds the split into `input_feature` and appends a size-1 spatial dimension, turning a 2D convolution into a 3D spatial convolution. For small-channel 2D backward-weight convolutions that can be lowered directly in a spatial-minor layout, this rank change prevents downstream rewrites from matching the convolution and forces a fallback to spatial-major layouts with expensive layout-conversion copies.

So this change adds `disable_backprop_filter_propagation_max_feature_size` to `SpaceToBatchController` in `xla/service/space_to_batch_converter.h` to skip propagating space-to-batch splits into eligible small-channel 2D backward-weight convolutions, while continuing to propagate splits into unstrided, high-padded, and large-channel convolutions.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1018243846

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject side-effecting instructions inside `map` subcomputations in `HloVerifier`.

Check in `InstructionVerifier::HandleMap` that computations reachable from
`kMap::to_apply()` (including nested control-flow computations such as `while`
bodies or `conditional` branches) do not contain side-effecting instructions.
Track verified computations on `InstructionVerifier` and check
`HasSideEffectNoRecurse()` so modules without `map` do no extra work and shared
subcomputations are scanned at most once per module.

head_commit.message:
PR #52725: [XLA:GPU] Expose ROCm's libhipcxx from include/hipccl as its own include root

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52725

Motivation
As part of the move to the CCCL 3.0-3.3 API, AMD is introducing hipCCL, a
unified package for rocPRIM, hipCUB and rocThrust that mirrors the role
NVIDIA's CCCL plays for CUB, Thrust and libcu++. hipCCL installs libhipcxx under `<rocm>/include/hipccl`, which Bazel did not expose, so hipCUB could fail with 'libhipcxx could not be found'.

📝 Summary of Changes
This change works with both the legacy and the new (upcoming) hipccl layouts. It adds `:rocm_libhipcxx_includes`, which strips `include/hipccl` so the headers
are reachable by hipCUB, and depends on it from `:rocm_headers_includes`.

The glob covers the whole directory rather than naming subdirectories, because
libhipcxx headers cross-reference each other across cuda/, hip/, nv/ and
amd/. `allow_empty` leaves ROCm installs without `include/hipccl` unchanged.

🎯 Justification
This change is important to avoid build failures with ROCm's planned migration to hipCCL 3.x.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
N/A

🧪 Unit Tests:
Tested by building XLA in two ROCm containers:
- libhipcxx alone under include/hipccl, with hipCUB/rocPRIM/rocThrust in
include/
- the hipCCL layout, where hipCUB/rocPRIM/rocThrust are under include/hipccl too and include/{hipcub,rocprim,rocthrust} are symlinks into it

No unit tests were added.

🧪 Execution Tests:
N/A

Reviewed and approved for AMD by the ROCm XLA team in ROCm/xla#1419.

display_title: [XLA] Do not inline `map` computations rooted at control-flow instructions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Do not inline `map` computations rooted at `while`, `conditional`, or `call`.

`MapInliner` currently skips `kFusion` roots when all operands are parameters,
but still tries to clone `kWhile`, `kConditional`, and `kCall` roots directly to
the tensor shape of the enclosing `map`. Cloning those control-flow instructions
to a non-scalar shape produces invalid HLO (and for `while`, tensor-wide loop
termination does not match per-element `map` semantics). Skip inlining them in
the same way as `kFusion`.

- RocmExecutor::IsHostMemoryPinned left start_addr/range_size

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Support CTA cluster synchronization in bitonic sort

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support CTA cluster synchronization in bitonic sort

Previously, the MLIR bitonic sort emitter only fused compare-and-swap steps
within one CTA's shared-memory tile (`tile_size`), requiring a separate global
kernel launch per step once `xor_mask >= tile_size`.

On Hopper+ GPUs (`sm_90+`), extend tiled bitonic sort across 2-CTA clusters
using distributed shared memory (DSMEM) and cluster barriers, doubling the
in-kernel sort span and cutting global round-trips:
- Propagate optional `se::ClusterDim` through `LaunchDimensions` and custom
  kernel specs to set driver cluster dims and `"nvvm.cluster_dim"` on kernels.
- Add `gpu::BarrierScope` (default `Workgroup`) to `xla_gpu.sync_threads`,
  forward it to `gpu.barrier` in `LowerTensors`, and lower cluster barriers to
  aligned `nvvm.cluster.arrive` and `nvvm.cluster.wait` in `LowerToLLVMGPU`.
- Support `"xla_gpu.dsmem"` on shared-memory accesses in `LowerTensors` by
  mapping the base pointer to the peer CTA's shared memory via `nvvm.mapa`.
- Emit 2-CTA clustered bitonic sort kernels when stages exceed `tile_size`,
  unclustered blocks exceed SM count, and cluster padding is at most 12.5%
  (capping at 2 CTAs avoids GPC fragmentation and register pressure). Cross-CTA
  steps use `gpu.cluster_block_id x` and DSMEM; full tiles keep the unrolled
  fast path while bounds-checked and post-cluster `kIntraTileSort` merges stay
  rolled.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013688390

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reorder `all-gather(broadcast)` when only the gather dimension is broadcast

`MatchAllGatherBroadcastReorder` in
`xla/hlo/transforms/collectives/all_gather_broadcast_reorder.cc` inserted
`all_gather_dimension` into `non_uniform_dims` and computed `uniform_dim_size`
from the `all-gather` output shape, ignoring broadcast repetition along the
gather dimension itself. Compute `uniform_dim_size` over the `broadcast` output
dimensions not in `bcast->dimensions()` so broadcasts repeating only along
`all_gather_dimension` are reordered to shrink the `all-gather`.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/50671.

display_title: [XLA] Avoid propagating or querying tile counts on `{unreduced}` shardings

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Avoid propagating or querying tile counts on `{unreduced}` shardings

`IsLeafShardingMoreSpecific` previously checked `IsManualLeaf()` and `IsReplicatedOrSingleDeviceLeaf()` before calling `NumTiles()`, hitting `CHECK(IsTiledLeaf())` in `TiledDataRank()` when encountering `{unreduced}` (or `{unknown}`) leaf shardings during `PickRepresentativeOperand`. In addition, `IsSpatiallyPartitioned` and `ReturnImprovedShardingImpl` did not exclude unreduced shardings, allowing GSPMD `ShardingPropagation` to treat `{unreduced}` operands as spatially partitioned candidates for arbitrary operations.

Guard `IsLeafShardingMoreSpecific`, `ReturnImprovedShardingImpl`, `UntileLeafShape`, `IsSpatiallyPartitioned`, and `PickRepresentativeOperand` against unreduced and unknown shardings so they neither crash on `NumTiles()` nor propagate `{unreduced}` across unsupported operations while still allowing valid tiled operands to propagate.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/50824.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1018969077
