display_title: Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

head_commit.message:
Cache XLA LocalClient instances by allowed_devices

`ClientLibrary::GetOrCreateLocalClient` previously keyed `local_instances_` only on `platform->id()`, ignoring `options.allowed_devices()` on cache hits. When multiple `PjRtClient` instances (or TensorFlow and PJRT clients) were created in the same process with different `allowed_devices` sets, every call after the first received the first call's `LocalClient` and its `StreamExecutor` list.

Therefore this change keys `ClientLibrary::local_instances_` by `(platform->id(), options.allowed_devices())` so each `allowed_devices` configuration gets a `LocalClient` restricted to those devices, while `DestroyLocalInstance(platform)` still clears all cached instances for that platform. It also:
- Updates `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient::UpdateCompileOptions` to fall back to `client()->default_device_ordinal()` instead of hardcoding device ordinal `0`, which fails when `allowed_devices` does not include device `0`.
- Forwards `visible_devices` in `GetTargetConfigFromOptions` (`xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_gpu_internal.cc`) when creating a GPU topology description via the PJRT C API.
- Preserves `allowed_devices` in `XlaDevice::Metadata` when looking up the `LocalClient`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Fix heap-use-after-free when iterating computations in `ReduceWindowRewriter`

`ReduceWindowRewriter::RunImpl` iterated lazily over
`module->computations(execution_threads)` while rewriting variadic cumulative
`reduce-window` ops via `RewriteScanAsTreeReduction`, which calls
`HloModule::AddEmbeddedComputation` and can reallocate `HloModule::computations_`.
Iterate over `module->MakeNonfusionComputations(execution_threads)` instead,
matching `AssociativeScanRewriter::RunImpl`.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/49822.

display_title: PR #52240: [XLA:GPU] Preserve frontend attributes in dot rewriters

head_commit.message:
PR #52240: [XLA:GPU] Preserve frontend attributes in dot rewriters

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52240

:pencil: **Summary of Changes**

Preserve frontend attributes when dot rewriters replace a dot with new instructions. New dots are added with `HloInstruction::AddInstruction` on the original dot, which derives them via `SetupDerivedInstruction` (also carrying metadata and, where shapes allow, sharding, like existing rewriters such as `DotDimensionSorter`), so they inherit the original dot's frontend attributes instead of silently dropping them. This covers `DotAlgorithmRewriter` (the BF16/TF32 decompositions in `backends/gpu/transforms` and the FP8xN decomposition in `hlo/transforms/dot_algorithm_rewriter.cc`), `ScaledDotRewriter`, `SplitkRewriter`, and `GemmFusionSwapOperands`.

:dart: **Justification**

Frontend attributes are the mechanism by which the frontend (e.g. JAX) attaches annotations to HLO instructions for downstream passes to consume. When a pass replaces an instruction, it must carry those attributes over to the replacement; otherwise the annotation is silently dropped and the consumers that depend on it no longer see it. These dot rewriters were not doing this, so annotated matmuls lost their scheduling annotations.

:compass: **Design: deriving replacements from the original dot**

Each new dot is added with `original_dot->AddInstruction(...)`, which derives it via `SetupDerivedInstruction` (metadata, frontend attributes, and sharding where the shapes allow). Instructions built by helpers call `SetupDerivedInstruction` directly: the instruction that replaces the dot in `RewriteDotWithOperandPairs` (shared by BF16X3/X6/X9 and TF32X3) and `RewriteFp8xNDot` (FP8X3/X4), and the split-K dot, which `MakeDotHlo` creates. So every new dot and the instruction that replaces the original keep the annotation.

:rocket: **Kind of Contribution**

:bug: Bug Fix

:test_tube: **Unit Tests:**

Added hardware-independent tests asserting frontend attributes survive each dot rewrite:

* `backends/gpu/transforms/dot_algorithm_rewriter_test.cc`:
  * `KeepsFrontendAttributes`, parameterized over every `PrecisionConfig::Algorithm`: verifies that after the pass every dot and the instruction that replaces the dot keep the attributes. Without the fix it fails for the seven algorithms the pass decomposes (BF16, BF16X3/X6/X9, TF32X3, FP8X3/X4); new algorithms are covered automatically.
* `hlo/transforms/dot_algorithm_rewriter_test.cc`:
  * `RewriteFp8xNDotStructureTest.KeepsFrontendAttributes`, for FP8X3 and FP8X4 at both precisions: verifies every F8 dot and the instruction that replaces the dot keep them.
* `gemm_fusion_swap_operands_test.cc`:
  * `SwappedDotKeepsFrontendAttributes`: verifies the swapped dot keeps them.
* `scaled_dot_rewriter_test.cc`:
  * `RewrittenDotKeepsFrontendAttributes`: verifies the dot replacing a scaled-dot keeps them.
* `splitk_rewriter_test.cc`:
  * `SplitKDotKeepsFrontendAttributes`: verifies the split-K dot keeps them.

:test_tube: **Execution Tests:**

No new checked-in execution test was added.

display_title: [XLA] Reorder `all-gather(broadcast)` when only the gather dimension is broadcast

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reorder `all-gather(broadcast)` when only the gather dimension is broadcast

`MatchAllGatherBroadcastReorder` in
`xla/hlo/transforms/collectives/all_gather_broadcast_reorder.cc` inserted
`all_gather_dimension` into `non_uniform_dims` and computed `uniform_dim_size`
from the `all-gather` output shape, ignoring broadcast repetition along the
gather dimension itself. Compute `uniform_dim_size` over the `broadcast` output
dimensions not in `bcast->dimensions()` so broadcasts repeating only along
`all_gather_dimension` are reordered to shrink the `all-gather`.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/50671.

display_title: PR #52508: Skip main-thread async computations from layout normalization

head_commit.message:
PR #52508: Skip main-thread async computations from layout normalization

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52508

📝 Summary of Changes

`LayoutNormalization` can currently insert bitcasts into async `HloComputations` that must contain only parameter instructions and a root. This causes the output HLO to fail verification (the HLO verifier requires main-thread async computations to contain only parameter instructions and a root, unless they have a unique caller annotated with `_collectives_group`). This PR makes `LayoutNormalization` skip main-thread async computations other than collectives groups (async-start marked with `_collectives_group`) to prevent bitcasts from being inserted into single-instruction async computations.

This follows the fix recommended by the reviewer in [XLA#51372](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51372) as an alternative to XLA#51372's post-pass legalization.

🎯 Justification

Currently, valid input HLO containing async computations can become invalid during layout normalization, causing subsequent HLO verification to fail compilation. The added tests include HLO that triggers this issue.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests

Added to `layout_normalization_test.cc`:

- `NoBitcastsInMainThreadAsyncComputation`: runs layout normalization on a main-thread async computation and checks with the layout-sensitive verifier that no bitcasts were inserted into the body. The caller is still normalized.
- `NonMainThreadAsyncComputationIsNormalized`: an async computation on a non-main execution thread is still normalized and verifies.
- `CollectivesGroupAsyncComputationIsNormalized`: a multi-instruction collectives group computation is still normalized.

🧪 Execution Tests

Execution tests with 3 different MaxText recipes across 1–2 GB300 nodes show no meaningful changes in performance or final loss. Furthermore, the HLO after optimization and thunk sequences are identical between baseline and test runs for all three recipes.

The recipes below use the same training arguments and runtime XLA flags as described [here](https://gist.github.com/rao-ashish/4d01922faf917d7c341c61cdb6a8e3f5). The baseline uses XLA commit `f824cdd4dc` and the test uses `adf4d527a2`. Both use the same JAX revision (`70b48fe198`) and MaxText revision (`d068d3383b`).

| model_name | variant_name | num_gpus | last_10_steps_median_tflops_per_sec | final_loss |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| llama3-8b | baseline | 4 (1 nodes) | 1362.123069 | 0.107112 |
| llama3-8b | test | 4 (1 nodes) | 1369.315992 | 0.106816 |
| gemma3-27b | baseline | 8 (2 nodes) | 1188.809494 | 0.131481 |
| gemma3-27b | test | 8 (2 nodes) | 1189.833898 | 0.131518 |
| mixtral-8x7b | baseline | 8 (2 nodes) | 367.691374 | 7.594059 |
| mixtral-8x7b | test | 8 (2 nodes) | 367.668602 | 7.600986 |

head_commit.message:
PR #51724: [XLA:GPU] Add locality-domain placement to the CUDA device allocator

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51724

📝 Summary of Changes

Implements the allocator layer that later PRs build the per-domain BFC pools on.

Adds `StreamExecutor::CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocator(int locality_domain_id)`, which returns a MemoryAllocator whose physical memory is placed on one locality domain (die) of a multi-die GPU.

CUDA implementation: `locality_domain_id` added to `CudaDeviceAllocator::Options`. When it's set, the allocator creates physical memory with `cuMemCreate` with location set to `CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE_LOCALITY_DOMAIN`.

Errors instead of fallback: it rejects out-of-range domain IDs, CUDA older than 13.4, single-domain devices, and the cuMemAlloc path (use_vmm=false). It never falls back to whole-device memory.

🎯 Justification

This is the third PR in the locality-domain series ([first](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50131) and [second](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51429) PRs)

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature and 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A: this PR adds the allocator only. Performance benefits to be evaluated later.

🧪 Unit Tests:
- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.RejectsOutOfRangeLocalityDomain`: domain IDs below -1 or above 255 are rejected.
- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.LocalityDomainRequiresCuda134`: CUDA older than 13.4 is rejected.
- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.LocalityDomainRequiresVmm`: use_vmm=false is rejected.
- `CudaExecutorTest.CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocatorRejectsInvalidId`: IDs outside [0, domain_count) are rejected.
- `DeviceAddressVmmAllocatorTest.RejectsLocalityDomainMemorySpaces`: locality-domain colors are rejected on every allocation path.

🧪 Execution Tests:
Both run on a single GPU:

- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.PlacesMemoryOnEachDomain`: for each domain, allocates memory and checks with `cuMemGetAllocationPropertiesFromHandle` that its location is `CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE_LOCALITY_DOMAIN` with the requested domain ID. Then it round-trips data host to device to host.
- `CudaExecutorTest.CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocatorWorks`: creates an allocator for every domain and allocates from it. On a single-domain GPU, it checks that creating one fails.

display_title: Chunk sub-byte sub-tile packing in tiled linearizer.

head_commit.message:
Chunk sub-tile packing and unpacking in tiled linearizer

Linearizing and delinearizing sub-tile-packed tensors previously allocated a temporary buffer spanning the entire unpacked array. Large sub-byte arrays caused tens of gigabytes of unreserved host memory growth.

This change transposes and repacks sub-tile-packed data in bounded cache-sized chunks of one to two megabytes. Both host-to-device linearization and device-to-host delinearization now reuse a small scratch buffer while preserving parallel execution.

head_commit.message:
PR #52508: Skip main-thread async computations from layout normalization

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52508

📝 Summary of Changes

`LayoutNormalization` can currently insert bitcasts into async `HloComputations` that must contain only parameter instructions and a root. This causes the output HLO to fail verification (the HLO verifier requires main-thread async computations to contain only parameter instructions and a root, unless they have a unique caller annotated with `_collectives_group`). This PR makes `LayoutNormalization` skip main-thread async computations other than collectives groups (async-start marked with `_collectives_group`) to prevent bitcasts from being inserted into single-instruction async computations.

This follows the fix recommended by the reviewer in [XLA#51372](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51372) as an alternative to XLA#51372's post-pass legalization.

🎯 Justification

Currently, valid input HLO containing async computations can become invalid during layout normalization, causing subsequent HLO verification to fail compilation. The added tests include HLO that triggers this issue.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests

Added to `layout_normalization_test.cc`:

- `NoBitcastsInMainThreadAsyncComputation`: runs layout normalization on a main-thread async computation and checks with the layout-sensitive verifier that no bitcasts were inserted into the body. The caller is still normalized.
- `NonMainThreadAsyncComputationIsNormalized`: an async computation on a non-main execution thread is still normalized and verifies.
- `CollectivesGroupAsyncComputationIsNormalized`: a multi-instruction collectives group computation is still normalized.

🧪 Execution Tests

Execution tests with 3 different MaxText recipes across 1–2 GB300 nodes show no meaningful changes in performance or final loss. Furthermore, the HLO after optimization and thunk sequences are identical between baseline and test runs for all three recipes.

The recipes below use the same training arguments and runtime XLA flags as described [here](https://gist.github.com/rao-ashish/4d01922faf917d7c341c61cdb6a8e3f5). The baseline uses XLA commit `f824cdd4dc` and the test uses `adf4d527a2`. Both use the same JAX revision (`70b48fe198`) and MaxText revision (`d068d3383b`).

display_title: Propagate C-order {2,1,0} layout to 3D ragged_dot args and outputs

head_commit.message:
Propagate C-order {2,1,0} layout to 3D ragged_dot args and outputs

## Description

* Layout pullback and bounded dynamism: When a 3D operand is transposed via
  `{0, 2, 1}` before `chlo.ragged_dot` (which expects `{2, 1, 0}`), the layout
  before transpose is pulled back via `M_X[k] = P[M_Y[k]]` to `{1, 2, 0}`.
  Operand seeding targets rank 3 RHS operands (`rhs_group_dimensions[0] == 0`)
  and 3D results, passing through `stablehlo.set_dimension_size`, mapping
  arguments via `@main` block arg indices, and skipping custom annotations when
  dynamic pad/slice adapters run.
* Buffer lifetime and adoption safety: `EnqueueExecutable` drains active device
  streams via `MaterializeDevice` and synchronizes before adopting an
  unaliased, undonated default layout 3D parameter via
  `AdoptMaterializedBufferFrom`, while async transfer callers retain shared
  ownership via `GetSharedBuffer()`. `DeviceBufferList::Data` uses
  `buffers_mutex_` when adoption may occur (rank 3) and reads without locking
  after materialization otherwise.
* Output layout propagation on cache hits: `CompilationCache` records only
  genuinely custom output layouts into `SharedOutputLayouts` (deriving physical
  tiles via `GetDefaultLayout`). `ExecutionTask::FromTraversal` stamps them onto
  outputs unless a slicing postamble adapter is active. `MakeShared` checks
  `HloModule` result staticness, and `compiled_mode.cc` restores PJRT output
  layouts for dynamic or shrunk outputs.
* Selective 3D scan and relayout cache: `MlirRequires3DParamLayoutScan` and
  `Param3DLayoutScanPolicy` skip 3D parameter scanning when modules lack
  `chlo.ragged_dot`, 3D `mhlo.layout_mode`, or explicit `argument_layouts`.
  Unadopted relayout buffers are cached only after materialization completes
  (`GetMaterializationFuture().Await()`) and evicted on error, deletion, or
  donation.
* XLA dynamic ragged dot and dynamism fixes: `HandleRaggedDot` in
  `dynamic_dimension_inference.cc` handles `kContracting` output offsets and

display_title: Propagate C-order {2,1,0} layout to 3D ragged_dot args and outputs

head_commit.message:
Propagate C-order {2,1,0} layout to 3D ragged_dot args and outputs

## Description

* Layout pullback and bounded dynamism: When a 3D operand is transposed via
  `{0, 2, 1}` before `chlo.ragged_dot` (which expects `{2, 1, 0}`), the layout
  before transpose is pulled back via `M_X[k] = P[M_Y[k]]` to `{1, 2, 0}`.
  Operand seeding targets rank 3 RHS operands (`rhs_group_dimensions[0] == 0`)
  and 3D results, passing through `stablehlo.set_dimension_size`, mapping
  arguments via `@main` block arg indices, and skipping custom annotations when
  dynamic pad/slice adapters run.
* Buffer lifetime and adoption safety: `EnqueueExecutable` drains active device
  streams via `MaterializeDevice` and synchronizes before adopting an
  unaliased, undonated default layout 3D parameter via
  `AdoptMaterializedBufferFrom`, while async transfer callers retain shared
  ownership via `GetSharedBuffer()`. `DeviceBufferList::Data` uses
  `buffers_mutex_` when adoption may occur (rank 3) and reads without locking
  after materialization otherwise.
* Output layout propagation on cache hits: `CompilationCache` records only
  genuinely custom output layouts into `SharedOutputLayouts` (deriving physical
  tiles via `GetDefaultLayout`). `ExecutionTask::FromTraversal` stamps them onto
  outputs unless a slicing postamble adapter is active. `MakeShared` checks
  `HloModule` result staticness, and `compiled_mode.cc` restores PJRT output
  layouts for dynamic or shrunk outputs.
* Selective 3D scan and relayout cache: `MlirRequires3DParamLayoutScan` and
  `Param3DLayoutScanPolicy` skip 3D parameter scanning when modules lack
  `chlo.ragged_dot`, 3D `mhlo.layout_mode`, or explicit `argument_layouts`.
  Unadopted relayout buffers are cached only after materialization completes
  (`GetMaterializationFuture().Await()`) and evicted on error, deletion, or
  donation.
* XLA dynamic ragged dot and dynamism fixes: `HandleRaggedDot` in
  `dynamic_dimension_inference.cc` handles `kContracting` output offsets and
  `group_sizes`, `DynamicPadder::ChooseIdentityValue` uses each operand dtype
  for `kRaggedDot`, `GetDynamismInfo` returns dynamic dimensions by value, and
  host to device transfers skip `GetDefaultLayout` without layout overrides.

display_title: [PJRT] Add thread-safe FFI context attachment on PjRtMemorySpace

head_commit.message:
[PJRT] Add thread-safe FFI context attachment on PjRtMemorySpace

Adds `SetFfiContext`, `UnsetFfiContext`, and `GetFfiContext` on `xla::PjRtMemorySpace` so host-offloaded FFI handlers that receive direct device buffers (`PjRtRawBuffer`) can resolve caller-owned execution context objects registered on the buffer's `PjRtMemorySpace` without mutating `PjRtMemorySpaceCApiDelegator::user_data_` or relying on process-level singletons:
- `SetFfiContext(const void* key, std::weak_ptr<void> context)` registers a weakly-referenced context object keyed by a caller-owned tag address (`const void* key`), delegating through `FromC(ToCApiPtr())` when called on a C-API wrapper `PjRtMemorySpace` and returning `AlreadyExistsError` if a different live object is currently registered under `key` while allowing idempotent re-registration and overwriting expired entries.
- `UnsetFfiContext(const void* key, const void* expected_context = nullptr)` unregisters the entry under `ffi_context_mu_`.
- `GetFfiContext(const void* key)` locks and returns the `std::shared_ptr<void>` under a reader lock (`absl::ReaderMutexLock`), returning `nullptr` if unregistered or expired.

display_title: [XLA] Use priority_for_operand for mandatory output to operand propagation

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Use priority_for_operand for mandatory output to operand propagation

`LayoutAssignment::PropagateBufferConstraintToOperands` marks derived operand
layouts mandatory for `HloOpcode::kBroadcast`, rank changing
`HloOpcode::kBitcastConvert`, and when `OutputLayoutAlwaysPropagateToOperands`
returns true. Previously, `kBroadcast` and mandatory
`OutputLayoutAlwaysPropagateToOperands` passed raw `priority` instead of
elevating priority over existing mandatory operand constraints, rank changing
`kBitcastConvert` derived the operand layout from `instruction->shape()` rather
than `buffer_constraint.layout()`, `priority_for_operand` copied priority from
non mandatory hints, and `OperandLayoutConstraint::UpdateLayout` rejected
`!mandatory_ && mandatory` upgrades when `priority() > new_priority`.

Allow `OperandLayoutConstraint::UpdateLayout` to upgrade non mandatory operand
constraints to mandatory at `new_priority` without carrying over the rejected
hint priority. Restrict `priority_for_operand` to existing mandatory operand
constraints, apply `buffer_constraint.layout()` on rank changing
`kBitcastConvert`, and elevate mandatory priority across `kBroadcast` and
`OutputLayoutAlwaysPropagateToOperands`. Covered by unit tests in
`layout_assignment_test.cc`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019679721

[TF] Remove `rules_python_local_wheel.patch` in favor of `local_wheel_repo`.

Replace the `rules_python_local_wheel.patch` `single_version_override` and the
custom `pip.parse(local_wheels = ...)` attribute with a self-contained Starlark
repository rule (`local_wheel_repo` / `@local_tf_wheel`). Under Bzlmod,
`single_version_override` is ignored for non-root modules, so downstream
projects depending on TensorFlow via `MODULE.bazel` saw unpatched `rules_python`
and failed with `unknown attribute local_wheels provided`.

* Delete `third_party/py/rules_python_local_wheel.patch` and remove it along
  with `pip.parse(local_wheels = ...)` from `MODULE.bazel`.
* Add `third_party/extensions/local_wheel.bzl` (`local_wheel_repo`), a lazy,
  non-reproducible repository rule exposing `dist/<WHEEL_NAME>-*.whl` as
  `@local_tf_wheel//:whl` (watches `dist/` for incremental rebuilds, supports
  hyphen/underscore `WHEEL_NAME` variants, and safely produces an empty
  `filegroup` when `dist/` is absent).
* Update `tf_wheel_dep()` in `tensorflow/tools/pip_package/utils/tf_wheel.bzl`
  to return `@local_tf_wheel//:whl` under Bzlmod while keeping
  `@pypi//<WHEEL_NAME>:whl` under `--config=workspace`.

display_title: [XLA] Use priority_for_operand for mandatory output to operand propagation

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Use priority_for_operand for mandatory output to operand propagation

`LayoutAssignment::PropagateBufferConstraintToOperands` marks derived operand
layouts mandatory for `HloOpcode::kBroadcast`, rank changing
`HloOpcode::kBitcastConvert`, and when `OutputLayoutAlwaysPropagateToOperands`
returns true. Previously, `kBroadcast` and mandatory
`OutputLayoutAlwaysPropagateToOperands` passed raw `priority` instead of
elevating priority over existing mandatory operand constraints, rank changing
`kBitcastConvert` derived the operand layout from `instruction->shape()` rather
than `buffer_constraint.layout()`, `priority_for_operand` copied priority from
non mandatory hints, and `OperandLayoutConstraint::UpdateLayout` rejected
`!mandatory_ && mandatory` upgrades when `priority() > new_priority`.

Allow `OperandLayoutConstraint::UpdateLayout` to upgrade non mandatory operand
constraints to mandatory at `new_priority` without carrying over the rejected
hint priority. Restrict `priority_for_operand` to existing mandatory operand
constraints, apply `buffer_constraint.layout()` on rank changing
`kBitcastConvert`, and elevate mandatory priority across `kBroadcast` and
`OutputLayoutAlwaysPropagateToOperands`. Covered by unit tests in
`layout_assignment_test.cc`.

display_title: [PJRT] Add thread-safe FFI context attachment on PjRtMemorySpace

head_commit.message:
[PJRT] Add thread-safe FFI context attachment on PjRtMemorySpace

Adds `SetFfiContext`, `UnsetFfiContext`, and `GetFfiContext` on `xla::PjRtMemorySpace` so host-offloaded FFI handlers that receive direct device buffers (`PjRtRawBuffer`) can resolve caller-owned execution context objects registered on the buffer's `PjRtMemorySpace` without mutating `PjRtMemorySpaceCApiDelegator::user_data_` or relying on process-level singletons:
- `SetFfiContext(const void* key, std::weak_ptr<void> context)` registers a weakly-referenced context object keyed by a caller-owned tag address (`const void* key`), delegating through `FromC(ToCApiPtr())` when called on a C-API wrapper `PjRtMemorySpace` and returning `AlreadyExistsError` if a different live object is currently registered under `key` while allowing idempotent re-registration and overwriting expired entries.
- `UnsetFfiContext(const void* key, const void* expected_context = nullptr)` unregisters the entry under `ffi_context_mu_`.
- `GetFfiContext(const void* key)` locks and returns the `std::shared_ptr<void>` under a reader lock (`absl::ReaderMutexLock`), returning `nullptr` if unregistered or expired.

display_title: Keep top-k sorts that the sort prefix sublane select lowers faster.

head_commit.message:
Keep top-k sorts that the sort prefix sublane select lowers faster.

The rank-2 `TpuTopkRewriter` cost model compares a `TopK` custom call with a
full sort. A top-`k` prefix of rows of 256 or 512 keys never lowers as one:
`SortPrefixEmitter` takes it through the sublane select, which costs about one
column of 128 rows. The `TopK` call pays for every row block, so `jax.lax.top_k`
sends small `k` over many rows to a slower lowering.

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Cap the number of operands of a loop fusion

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Cap the number of operands of a loop fusion

`CpuInstructionFusion` has no bound on how large a loop fusion may grow. The only size-related guard, `FusionNodeIndexingEvaluation::CodeDuplicationTooHigh`, is skipped entirely when the pass runs with `may_duplicate=false`, which `cpu_compiler.cc` selects whenever `xla_cpu_use_multi_output_fusion` is set.

On reverse-mode AD programs of stencil codes (Enzyme-MLIR / Reactant differentiating the Oceananigans ocean model) this produces loop fusions with 210–250 operands and 880–1045 fused instructions per output element: the `pad`-accumulate chain of every halo'd adjoint pulls in each stencil tap's whole producer DAG. The elemental emitter's per-element code for such a fusion neither vectorizes nor fits in registers; the reverse loop ran ~10× the primal while doing 4.2× its FLOPs.

This change adds an operand budget, checked independently of `may_duplicate()`: a producer is not fused into an existing fusion if the result would have more than `xla_cpu_max_fusion_operands` distinct operands (default 96, matching the GPU backend's `MaxOperandsAndOutputsPerFusion`). The option is an `xla_backend_extra_options` entry read through `cpu_options`; a value `<= 0` disables the check.

The budget is deliberately on operands only. An earlier revision also capped the number of fused instructions (512), which split long single-input elementwise chains and changed numerics in two JAX CPU tests: (a) `jax.scipy.special.iv` (f32) is a 540-instruction chain using double-float arithmetic; XLA:CPU sets `contract` on all FP arithmetic, so a kernel boundary prevents FMA contraction across it and breaks the error-free transformations (1.36 ULP instead of ≤ 1). (b) `ndtri_exp` gradient (bf16) differs on subnormal inputs: XLA:CPU runs kernels with denormals-are-zero, but LLVM folds `y == 0` on a bf16→f32 convert into an integer test on the bits, while `y < 0` stays a `ucomiss` that honors DAZ; which fold applies depends on the kernel boundaries. Both effects are pre-existing properties of XLA:CPU that any change in fusion boundaries can expose; the operand cap alone does not split these chains (they have 1–13 operands) and does not change either test.

Measurements (Oceananigans channel-model gradient, 8 time steps, one x86 core, `xla_cpu_use_multi_output_fusion` on; min / median of 3 calls):

| operand cap | gradient | primal |
|---|---|---|
| unpatched | 28.1 / 28.9 s | 3.01 s |
| disabled (`0`, control) | 28.0 / 29.3 s | — |
| 128 | 17.4 / 17.7 s | — |
| 96 (default) | 13.8 / 14.2 s | 2.89 s |
| 64 | 14.8 / 14.9 s | — |
| 48 | 11.7–13.1 / 12.2–13.2 s | 2.37 s |
| 32 | 12.8 / 13.1 s | 2.19 s |

(The 48 row spans four runs with the earlier instruction cap at 512, 1024, 4096 and disabled: 13.0, 11.7, 12.8, 13.1 s min — the instruction cap had no measurable effect, which is why it was dropped.) Results are bit-identical in the objective and agree with the unpatched build to rel. L2 ≤ 2e-15 in every gradient field.

The default is 96 rather than 48 based on a sweep over a suite of 80 CPU benchmark HLO models (A/B against head, 20 runs each). Compiling every model at several caps shows that any cap from 48 to 128 changes the fused HLO of the same two models (every other model has at most 42 operands per fusion), whereas the TORAX plasma-simulation models have fusions of 49–267 operands and are sensitive to the exact value: at cap 48 three of them regress 2–5% in wall time on Granite Rapids (4–13% on AMD Rome), while at cap 96 none regresses by more than 1% and their geomean improves by 1.2% (Granite Rapids) / 2.6% (Rome). The two models affected at any cap are within ±2% at either value. Suite-wide, the cap leaves runtime unchanged (geomean −0.2%) and improves compile wall time by 2% at the cost of 2% more compile CPU time.

Tests: `cpu_instruction_fusion_test` gains five cases on a 120-tap pad/add chain: the default budget splits it (largest fusion exactly 96 operands), also with `may_duplicate=false`, the budget is configurable (16), disabling it fuses the whole chain into one fusion, and a malformed option value is rejected with `InvalidArgument`.

The same change is vendored as a patch in Enzyme-JAX (https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Enzyme-JAX/pull/3882, https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Enzyme-JAX/pull/3883).

display_title: [XLA] Avoid propagating or querying tile counts on `{unreduced}` shardings

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Avoid propagating or querying tile counts on `{unreduced}` shardings

`IsLeafShardingMoreSpecific` previously checked `IsManualLeaf()` and `IsReplicatedOrSingleDeviceLeaf()` before calling `NumTiles()`, hitting `CHECK(IsTiledLeaf())` in `TiledDataRank()` when encountering `{unreduced}` (or `{unknown}`) leaf shardings during `PickRepresentativeOperand`. In addition, `IsSpatiallyPartitioned` and `ReturnImprovedShardingImpl` did not exclude unreduced shardings, allowing GSPMD `ShardingPropagation` to treat `{unreduced}` operands as spatially partitioned candidates for arbitrary operations.

Guard `IsLeafShardingMoreSpecific`, `ReturnImprovedShardingImpl`, `UntileLeafShape`, `IsSpatiallyPartitioned`, and `PickRepresentativeOperand` against unreduced and unknown shardings so they neither crash on `NumTiles()` nor propagate `{unreduced}` across unsupported operations while still allowing valid tiled operands to propagate.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/50824.

display_title: [XLA] Handle late bound async-start DUS in the async chain output path

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Handle late bound async-start DUS in the async chain output path

Dataflow analysis crashes on a late bound `async-start` wrapping `dynamic-update-slice`. Such a start has no operands; its operands and output are bound on the `async-update`. `UpdateAsyncStartValueSet` special cased DUS starts and read `operand(0)` without checking that it exists.

The DUS case moves into `UpdateAsyncChainOutputValueSet`. A DUS start still forwards its destination operand to `{1}`, but only when the start has that operand; otherwise it falls back to the wrapped root and the existing bound checks skip the unbound output. The forwarding is required: without it, a loop carried DUS start feeds the wrapped result back into the shared destination parameter, which then has two values and fails in place aliasing.

display_title: PR #52733: [PJRT] Drop completed usage events in stream-based compaction mode

head_commit.message:
PR #52733: [PJRT] Drop completed usage events in stream-based compaction mode

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52733

Fixes jax-ml/jax#42433.

The GPU client uses stream-based usage-event compaction. In that mode `AddUsageEvent` appends any event whose definition stream isn’t known yet, and never trims the list. A copy’s source usage event is a linked promise that is only fulfilled later in `IntraClientCopyToWithDependencies`, so it always takes that path: every copy from a long-lived buffer adds one entry, and the CUDA event behind it, until the buffer is deleted.

This lets those events fall through to the trimming the non-stream branch already does: when the list is full, events that have completed (Ready or errored) are dropped before appending. A completed event has nothing left to wait for. Execute’s donation path already skips Ready events, and stream-based compaction already skips errored events when they’re added. Pending events are kept.

With the issue’s reproducer (100k `device_put` copies to `pinned_host`, RTX 4060 Ti), host memory in use went from 65.7 to 171.0 MiB before, and from 65.7 to 65.8 MiB after. New CPU, Host-platform and GPU tests fail without the change and pass with it.

Copybara import of the project:

--
f71825ada9572b7d1881fd219089b85501ea2bab by JonSnow1807 <JonSnow1807@users.noreply.github.com>:

[PJRT] Drop completed usage events in stream-based compaction mode

With use_stream_based_compaction, which the GPU client sets,
AbstractTrackedDeviceBuffer::AddUsageEvent merges a new usage event into
the existing entry for its definition stream. An event whose definition
stream is not known yet is appended, and nothing in that branch ever
removes entries. Only the other branch trims events that have completed.

The source usage event of a copy is such an event. CommonCopyToMemorySpace
creates it with CreateLinkedEventPromise, and the promise is only set later
in IntraClientCopyToWithDependencies. So every CopyToMemorySpace from a
long-lived buffer, e.g. jax.device_put to another device or to pinned_host,
adds one entry, and the entries keep their CUDA events alive until the
buffer is deleted or donated. jax-ml/jax#42433 measured about 1.1 KB of
host memory per copy and source shard, without a plateau.

When the vector is full, drop the entries that are Ready before appending,
like the other branch does. A Ready usage event has completed without an
error, so Delete and the donation paths have nothing left to wait for, and
Execute already skips Ready usage events when it donates a buffer. Pending
and errored entries are kept, so per-stream merging and error propagation
do not change.

--
b99ed14ae36a18becabd36c71ae4877bc61edcdb by JonSnow1807 <JonSnow1807@users.noreply.github.com>:

[PJRT] Share usage event trimming between the compaction modes

Events that stream-based compaction can't merge now fall through to the
trimming the other mode already does, instead of a copy of it. The trim
checks the event state through the device event interface rather than
async_value(), which is null for events that aren't local AsyncValues.

Merging this change closes #52733

display_title: [TF] Switch TensorFlow default build to Bzlmod and sync MODULE.bazel.

head_commit.message:
[TF] Switch TensorFlow default build to Bzlmod and sync MODULE.bazel.

Following the Bazel 8.8.2 upgrade, enable `--enable_bzlmod` and `--noenable_workspace` by default in TensorFlow while adding `--config=workspace` as a fallback configuration and flipping `ci/official/envs/bzlmod` to `--config workspace` so `WORKSPACE` continues to be tested in CI for downstream consumers. Also set `--experimental_repository_downloader_retries=5` and `common --experimental_downloader_config=bazel_downloader.cfg` (including BCR mirror fallback rules), add `--nobuild_runfile_links` to `common:rbe_base`, prepend Bzlmod canonical CUDA library paths to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` in `test:linux_cuda_13_wheel_test`, and disable `layering_check` on macOS (`common:macos`) to match Linux and Windows toolchains.

In `MODULE.bazel`, third-party Bzlmod extensions, and platform patches:
- Register the hermetic SYCL and ROCm C++ toolchains from `rules_ml_toolchain`, sync the CUDA, CCCL (`3.4.0`), NCCL (`nccl_redist_patched`), NVSHMEM, SYCL, local sysroot, and `libdrm` module extensions and XLA third-party repositories (including deduplicating `nccl_archive`, `nvtx_archive`, `png`, and `absl_py` from `tf_third_party`) with XLA's `MODULE.bazel` and `workspace2.bzl`, and align the root BCR module declarations (`pybind11_bazel` 3.0.0, `apple_support` 2.8.0, `rules_swift` 2.9.0, `googletest` 1.18.0, `highway` 1.4.0, `dev_dependency = True` on test-only modules `rules_webtesting`, `fuzztest`, and `libprotobuf-mutator`, and `repo_name = None` compatibility pins for `c-ares`, `eigen`, `grpc-java`, and `libpfm`).
- Configure multi-platform `pip.parse` wheels (`xla_pypi = "pypi"`, `local_wheels` overrides via `rules_python_local_wheel.patch`, `@pypi//{}:whl` in `tf_wheel.bzl`, and Python 3.14 freethreaded lockfile/platform support), `pythons_hub`, `python_version_repo` via `use_repo_rule` (with `REQUIREMENTS` lockfile support, `TF_PYTHON_VERSION` fallback, `-freethreaded`/`-ft` suffix handling, and removing the unused `python_version_ext` extension), reproducible module extensions (`reproducible = True` on `third_party_ext`, `googleapis_ext`, and `nccl_redist_ext`), `maven`, and Bzlmod Java repositories (`generated_rule_name` in `java_repos.bzl` and Guava/JSR305/ErrorProne repos), alias `@system_python//:python_headers` to `rules_python`'s hermetic headers in `bazel9.patch`, and update `nvidia_wheel_deps`, `requirements_lock_3_*.txt` (`protobuf==6.33.6`), and `code_check_full.bats` for Bzlmod.
- Add Bzlmod compatibility patch overrides (`pybind11_abseil.patch`, Windows DLL support in `protobuf/bazel9.patch`, `google_cloud_cpp.patch`, `rules_android.patch`, and `googletest:remove_alwayslink.patch`), update Windows protobuf symbol exports in `_pywrap_tensorflow.def`, and update `gpu_prim.h` and `where_op_gpu.cu.h` (`THRUST_VERSION >= 300200`) for CCCL 3.4.0 compatibility.

Follow-up CLs will clean up remaining legacy WORKSPACE artifacts and deprecated `BUILD.oss` `$(location)` make variables, migrate remaining `java_import_external` and `tf_third_party` repositories to BCR modules/`rules_jvm_external`, and re-enable Bazel 8 incompatible flags in `.bazelrc`.

display_title: Propagate C-order {2,1,0} layout to 3D ragged_dot args and outputs

head_commit.message:
Propagate C-order {2,1,0} layout to 3D ragged_dot args and outputs

## Description

* Layout pullback and bounded dynamism: When a 3D operand is transposed via
  `{0, 2, 1}` before `chlo.ragged_dot` (which expects `{2, 1, 0}`), the layout
  before transpose is pulled back via `M_X[k] = P[M_Y[k]]` to `{1, 2, 0}`.
  Operand seeding targets rank 3 RHS operands (`rhs_group_dimensions[0] == 0`)
  and 3D results, passing through `stablehlo.set_dimension_size`, mapping
  arguments via `@main` block arg indices, and skipping custom annotations when
  dynamic pad/slice adapters run.
* Buffer lifetime and adoption safety: `EnqueueExecutable` drains active device
  streams via `MaterializeDevice` and synchronizes before adopting an
  unaliased, undonated default layout 3D parameter via
  `AdoptMaterializedBufferFrom`, while async transfer callers retain shared
  ownership via `GetSharedBuffer()`. `DeviceBufferList::Data` uses
  `buffers_mutex_` when adoption may occur (rank 3) and reads without locking
  after materialization otherwise.
* Output layout propagation on cache hits: `CompilationCache` records only
  genuinely custom output layouts into `SharedOutputLayouts` (deriving physical
  tiles via `GetDefaultLayout`). `ExecutionTask::FromTraversal` stamps them onto
  outputs unless a slicing postamble adapter is active. `MakeShared` checks
  `HloModule` result staticness, and `compiled_mode.cc` restores PJRT output
  layouts for dynamic or shrunk outputs.
* Selective 3D scan and relayout cache: `MlirRequires3DParamLayoutScan` and
  `Param3DLayoutScanPolicy` skip 3D parameter scanning when modules lack

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Dynamically scale chunked PJRT host-device transfer pipeline depth from 4 to 8.

head_commit.message:
Dynamically scale chunked PJRT host-device transfer pipeline depth from 4 to 8.

With 2 MiB chunks, a static 4-stage pipeline (8 MiB ring buffer) underutilizes host transpose threads and PCIe DMA concurrency on multi-core TPU hosts for single-tensor transfers and synchronous `kImmutableOnlyDuringCall` transfers, whereas a static 8-stage pipeline increases staging ring buffer memory pressure and worker thread contention when multiple asynchronous transfers run concurrently.

Track active chunked H2D and D2H `PipelinedChunkedTransfer` instances via `PipelinedChunkedTransfer::ActiveCount(is_h2d)` in `xla/pjrt/common_pjrt_client.cc` and select `max_stages = (!sync && ActiveCount(is_h2d) > 0) ? kBaseStages : kMaxStages` (4 when concurrent async transfers are in flight, 8 for single transfers or synchronous `kImmutableOnlyDuringCall` transfers). If another chunked transfer in the same direction starts while an 8-stage transfer is in flight, `CompleteStage2Chunk` drains its active stages down to `kBaseStages = 4`.

Updated `ChunkedLinearizeAndDelinearizeRoundTrip` in `xla/pjrt/pjrt_client_test.cc` to use 4096-row shapes (> 16 MiB) to exercise 8-stage ring buffer wrap-around, and verified CPU and TPU PJRT unit test suites. On TPU v7x and TPU v6e 8-vCPU host-device transfer benchmarks across `nt = 1, 4, 8`, single-transfer (`nt = 1`) and synchronous `kImmutableOnlyDuringCall` throughput improves by 18%–58% on TPU v7x (e.g., 64 MiB F32 H2D 21.7 → 34.3 GB/s, H2D sync 22.1 → 34.8 GB/s, D2H 23.7 → 32.0 GB/s) and by up to 45% on TPU v6e while keeping multi-transfer (`nt = 4, 8`) throughput neutral or faster.

display_title: PR #51724: [XLA:GPU] Add locality-domain placement to the CUDA device allocator

head_commit.message:
PR #51724: [XLA:GPU] Add locality-domain placement to the CUDA device allocator

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51724

📝 Summary of Changes

Implements the allocator layer that later PRs build the per-domain BFC pools on.

Adds `StreamExecutor::CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocator(int locality_domain_id)`, which returns a MemoryAllocator whose physical memory is placed on one locality domain (die) of a multi-die GPU.

CUDA implementation: `locality_domain_id` added to `CudaDeviceAllocator::Options`. When it's set, the allocator creates physical memory with `cuMemCreate` with location set to `CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE_LOCALITY_DOMAIN`.

Errors instead of fallback: it rejects out-of-range domain IDs, CUDA older than 13.4, single-domain devices, and the cuMemAlloc path (use_vmm=false). It never falls back to whole-device memory.

🎯 Justification

This is the third PR in the locality-domain series ([first](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50131) and [second](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51429) PRs)

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature and 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A: this PR adds the allocator only. Performance benefits to be evaluated later.

🧪 Unit Tests:
- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.RejectsOutOfRangeLocalityDomain`: domain IDs below -1 or above 255 are rejected.
- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.LocalityDomainRequiresCuda134`: CUDA older than 13.4 is rejected.
- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.LocalityDomainRequiresVmm`: use_vmm=false is rejected.
- `CudaExecutorTest.CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocatorRejectsInvalidId`: IDs outside [0, domain_count) are rejected.
- `DeviceAddressVmmAllocatorTest.RejectsLocalityDomainMemorySpaces`: locality-domain colors are rejected on every allocation path.

🧪 Execution Tests:
Both run on a single GPU:

- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.PlacesMemoryOnEachDomain`: for each domain, allocates memory and checks with `cuMemGetAllocationPropertiesFromHandle` that its location is `CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE_LOCALITY_DOMAIN` with the requested domain ID. Then it round-trips data host to device to host.
- `CudaExecutorTest.CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocatorWorks`: creates an allocator for every domain and allocates from it. On a single-domain GPU, it checks that creating one fails.
Copybara import of the project:

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Guard ScanLoopAccumulatorInputUnification against live uses

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Guard ScanLoopAccumulatorInputUnification against live uses

`ScanLoopAccumulatorInputUnification` replaces uses of `input_gte_inner` inside
the inner scan loop body with the accumulator `acc` and rewrites the inner loop
init tuple so the accumulator slot receives the input buffer. Previously,
`FindAccumulatorInputPairs` and `UnifyAccumulatorWithInput` did not verify:

1. That `gte_user` (`dynamic-update-slice`) has a single user, does not read
   `acc` as its update operand, and appears only once in the inner body root
   tuple, and that `input_gte_inner` appears only once in the inner body root
   tuple.
2. That all `body_param` users are `get-tuple-element`, that the GTEs for
   `param_idx` and `input_idx_inner` are unique, and that the non root user of
   `input_gte_inner` is selected explicitly.
3. That all `while_instr` users are `get-tuple-element` with
   `tuple_index() != input_idx_inner`, that `while_init()` has a single user
   and is not the parent root, and that the parent computation has a `tuple`
   root and is a `while_body()`.

Enforce these invariants before unifying an accumulator with an input.

`ReduceWindowRewriter::RunImpl` iterated lazily over
`module->computations(execution_threads)` while rewriting variadic cumulative

`HloModule::AddEmbeddedComputation` and can reallocate `HloModule::computations_`.
Iterate over `module->MakeNonfusionComputations(execution_threads)` instead,

display_title: [XLA:TSL] Reject negative byte counts in SnappyInputStream

head_commit.message:
[XLA:TSL] Reject negative byte counts in SnappyInputStream

SnappyInputStream::ReadNBytes passed a negative bytes_to_read to
tstring::resize_uninitialized, which takes a size_t. A count of -1 hit
the __builtin_trap in TF_TString_ResizeUninitialized and killed the
process; other negative counts convert to a size of 2^63 or more.
BufferedInputStream and RandomAccessInputStream return InvalidArgument
for a negative count.

Return InvalidArgument from SnappyInputStream::ReadNBytes the same way,
before touching result. Add a test that a negative count is rejected.

Follow-up to #52502.

display_title: [XLA] Handle late bound async-start DUS in the async chain output path

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Drop the async-start DUS special case in HLO dataflow analysis

Dataflow analysis crashes on a late bound `async-start` wrapping `dynamic-update-slice`. Such a start has no operands; its operands and output are bound on the `async-update`. `UpdateAsyncStartValueSet` special cased DUS starts and forwarded `operand(0)` to output `{1}` without checking that either exists.

The special case is removed, so every `async-start` goes through `UpdateAsyncChainOutputValueSet` and takes `{1}` from the wrapped root, like other async ops. Its existing checks skip outputs that are not bound yet, which covers the late bound start. Alias analysis already places a DUS destination and its result in one buffer through the in place pairs, so the forwarding was not needed.

head_commit.message:
Dynamically scale chunked PJRT host-device transfer pipeline depth from 4 to 8.

With 2 MiB chunks, a static 4-stage pipeline (8 MiB ring buffer) underutilizes host transpose threads and PCIe DMA concurrency on multi-core TPU hosts for single-tensor transfers and synchronous `kImmutableOnlyDuringCall` transfers, whereas a static 8-stage pipeline increases staging ring buffer memory pressure and worker thread contention when multiple asynchronous transfers run concurrently.

Track active chunked H2D and D2H `PipelinedChunkedTransfer` instances via `PipelinedChunkedTransfer::ActiveCount(is_h2d)` in `xla/pjrt/common_pjrt_client.cc` and select `max_stages = (!sync && ActiveCount(is_h2d) > 0) ? kBaseStages : kMaxStages` (4 when concurrent async transfers are in flight, 8 for single transfers or synchronous `kImmutableOnlyDuringCall` transfers). If another chunked transfer in the same direction starts while an 8-stage transfer is in flight, `CompleteStage2Chunk` drains its active stages down to `kBaseStages = 4`.

Updated `ChunkedLinearizeAndDelinearizeRoundTrip` in `xla/pjrt/pjrt_client_test.cc` to use 4096-row shapes (> 16 MiB) to exercise 8-stage ring buffer wrap-around, and verified CPU and TPU PJRT unit test suites. On TPU v7x and TPU v6e 8-vCPU host-device transfer benchmarks across `nt = 1, 4, 8`, single-transfer (`nt = 1`) and synchronous `kImmutableOnlyDuringCall` throughput improves by 18%–58% on TPU v7x (e.g., 64 MiB F32 H2D 21.7 → 34.3 GB/s, H2D sync 22.1 → 34.8 GB/s, D2H 23.7 → 32.0 GB/s) and by up to 45% on TPU v6e while keeping multi-transfer (`nt = 4, 8`) throughput neutral or faster.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Vectorize small kLoop phases on Hopper and newer GPUs.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Vectorize small kLoop phases on Hopper and newer GPUs.

`ComputeLoopFusionConfig` disables loop unrolling and vectorization when the output element count is smaller than the total hardware thread capacity (`threads_per_core_limit * core_count`), forcing `unroll_factor = 1` for every small stage considered by `MultiPhaseFusion` and phased nodes in `ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion`. Inside phased fusions, leaving small `kLoop` stages unvectorized inflates block counts past the 8-block cluster limit or forces multi-block cluster barriers where vectorized threads would fit into a single block.

Allow `ComputeLoopFusionConfig`, `LoopFusion`, and `ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion::CreateNativeNestedEmitter` to opt into unrolling small fusions via `unroll_small_inputs` / `unroll_small_fusions`, and enable it on Hopper and newer CUDA GPUs (`IsAtLeastHopper()`) in `MultiPhaseFusion` and for `kLoop` leaves inside phased nodes of `ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion`.

Also set `--experimental_repository_downloader_retries=5` and `common --experimental_downloader_config=bazel_downloader.cfg` (including BCR mirror fallback rules), add `--nobuild_runfile_links` to `common:rbe_base`, prepend Bzlmod canonical CUDA library paths to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` in `test:linux_cuda_13_wheel_test`, and disable `layering_check` on macOS (`common:macos`) to match Linux and Windows toolchains.

In `MODULE.bazel`, third-party Bzlmod extensions, and platform patches:
- Register the hermetic SYCL and ROCm C++ toolchains from `rules_ml_toolchain`, sync the CUDA, CCCL (`3.4.0`), NCCL (`nccl_redist_patched`), NVSHMEM, SYCL, local sysroot, and `libdrm` module extensions and XLA third-party repositories (including deduplicating `nccl_archive`, `nvtx_archive`, `png`, and `absl_py` from `tf_third_party`) with XLA's `MODULE.bazel` and `workspace2.bzl`, and align the root BCR module declarations (`pybind11_bazel` 3.0.0, `apple_support` 2.8.0, `rules_swift` 2.9.0, `googletest` 1.18.0, `highway` 1.4.0, `dev_dependency = True` on test-only modules `rules_webtesting`, `fuzztest`, and `libprotobuf-mutator`, and `repo_name = None` compatibility pins for `c-ares`, `eigen`, `grpc-java`, and `libpfm`).
- Configure multi-platform `pip.parse` wheels (`xla_pypi = "pypi"`, `local_wheels` overrides via `rules_python_local_wheel.patch`, `@pypi//{}:whl` in `tf_wheel.bzl`, and Python 3.14 freethreaded lockfile/platform support), `pythons_hub`, `python_version_repo` via `use_repo_rule` (with `REQUIREMENTS` lockfile support, `TF_PYTHON_VERSION` fallback, `-freethreaded`/`-ft` suffix handling, and removing the unused `python_version_ext` extension), reproducible module extensions (`reproducible = True` on `third_party_ext`, `googleapis_ext`, and `nccl_redist_ext`), `maven`, and Bzlmod Java repositories (`generated_rule_name` in `java_repos.bzl` and Guava/JSR305/ErrorProne repos), alias `@system_python//:python_headers` to `rules_python`'s hermetic headers in `bazel9.patch`, and update `nvidia_wheel_deps`, `requirements_lock_3_*.txt` (`protobuf==6.33.6`), and `code_check_full.bats` for Bzlmod.

display_title: [XLA] Remove every operand slot of an instruction fused into a callable

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Remove every operand slot of an instruction fused into a callable

A callable instruction can hold the same producer in several operand slots, for example after rematerialization replaces operands one slot at a time. `CloneAndAppendInstructionIntoCalledComputation` replaced the parameter of the first matching slot, stopped, and detached the callable from the producer. The other slots still referenced the producer, but its user list no longer named the callable. The next user removal on that edge failed the check in `HloInstruction::Users::UserId`, and deleting the dead producer left a stale operand pointer.

The loop now removes every matching parameter and operand slot before detaching the callable. It walks the operands in reverse, because each removal shifts only higher indices. Callables without repeated operands behave as before, and no flag is added.

Tests:
- `//third_party/tensorflow/compiler/xla/hlo/ir:hlo_instruction_test`: pins `FuseInstruction` of a producer that occupies two adjacent operand slots.

display_title: [XLA] Guard ScanLoopAccumulatorInputUnification against live uses

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Guard ScanLoopAccumulatorInputUnification against live uses

`ScanLoopAccumulatorInputUnification` replaces uses of `input_gte_inner` inside
the inner scan loop body with the accumulator `acc` and rewrites the inner loop
init tuple so the accumulator slot receives the input buffer. Previously,
`FindAccumulatorInputPairs` and `UnifyAccumulatorWithInput` did not verify:

1. That `gte_user` (`dynamic-update-slice`) has a single user, does not read
   `acc` as its update operand, and appears only once in the inner body root
   tuple, and that `input_gte_inner` appears only once in the inner body root
   tuple.
2. That all `body_param` users are `get-tuple-element`, that the GTEs for
   `param_idx` and `input_idx_inner` are unique, and that the non root user of
   `input_gte_inner` is selected explicitly.
3. That all `while_instr` users are `get-tuple-element` with
   `tuple_index() != input_idx_inner`, that `while_init()` has a single user
   and is not the parent root, and that the parent computation has a `tuple`
   root and is a `while_body()`.

Enforce these invariants before unifying an accumulator with an input.

display_title: PR #51724: [XLA:GPU] Add locality-domain placement to the CUDA device allocator

head_commit.message:
PR #51724: [XLA:GPU] Add locality-domain placement to the CUDA device allocator

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51724

📝 Summary of Changes

Implements the allocator layer that later PRs build the per-domain BFC pools on.

Adds `StreamExecutor::CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocator(int locality_domain_id)`, which returns a MemoryAllocator whose physical memory is placed on one locality domain (die) of a multi-die GPU.

CUDA implementation: `locality_domain_id` added to `CudaDeviceAllocator::Options`. When it's set, the allocator creates physical memory with `cuMemCreate` with location set to `CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE_LOCALITY_DOMAIN`.

Errors instead of fallback: it rejects out-of-range domain IDs, CUDA older than 13.4, single-domain devices, and the cuMemAlloc path (use_vmm=false). It never falls back to whole-device memory.

🎯 Justification

This is the third PR in the locality-domain series ([first](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50131) and [second](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51429) PRs)

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature and 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A: this PR adds the allocator only. Performance benefits to be evaluated later.

🧪 Unit Tests:
- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.RejectsOutOfRangeLocalityDomain`: domain IDs below -1 or above 255 are rejected.
- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.LocalityDomainRequiresCuda134`: CUDA older than 13.4 is rejected.
- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.LocalityDomainRequiresVmm`: use_vmm=false is rejected.
- `CudaExecutorTest.CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocatorRejectsInvalidId`: IDs outside [0, domain_count) are rejected.
- `DeviceAddressVmmAllocatorTest.RejectsLocalityDomainMemorySpaces`: locality-domain colors are rejected on every allocation path.

🧪 Execution Tests:
Both run on a single GPU:

- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.PlacesMemoryOnEachDomain`: for each domain, allocates memory and checks with `cuMemGetAllocationPropertiesFromHandle` that its location is `CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE_LOCALITY_DOMAIN` with the requested domain ID. Then it round-trips data host to device to host.
- `CudaExecutorTest.CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocatorWorks`: creates an allocator for every domain and allocates from it. On a single-domain GPU, it checks that creating one fails.
Copybara import of the project:

display_title: [XLA] Use priority_for_operand for mandatory output to operand propagation

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Use priority_for_operand for mandatory output to operand propagation

`LayoutAssignment::PropagateBufferConstraintToOperands` marks derived operand
layouts mandatory for `HloOpcode::kBroadcast`, rank changing
`HloOpcode::kBitcastConvert`, and when `OutputLayoutAlwaysPropagateToOperands`
returns true. Previously, `kBroadcast` and mandatory
`OutputLayoutAlwaysPropagateToOperands` passed raw `priority` instead of
elevating priority over existing mandatory operand constraints, rank changing
`kBitcastConvert` derived the operand layout from `instruction->shape()` rather
than `buffer_constraint.layout()`, `priority_for_operand` copied priority from
non mandatory hints, and `OperandLayoutConstraint::UpdateLayout` rejected
`!mandatory_ && mandatory` upgrades when `priority() > new_priority`.

Allow `OperandLayoutConstraint::UpdateLayout` to upgrade non mandatory operand
constraints to mandatory at `new_priority` without carrying over the rejected
hint priority. Restrict `priority_for_operand` to existing mandatory operand
constraints, apply `buffer_constraint.layout()` on rank changing
`kBitcastConvert`, and elevate mandatory priority across `kBroadcast` and
`OutputLayoutAlwaysPropagateToOperands`. Covered by unit tests in
`layout_assignment_test.cc`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Support scalar control flow in `map` and fuse `map` into `kLoop` kernels.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support scalar control flow in `map` and fuse `map` into `kLoop` kernels.

Support `map` instructions whose `to_apply` computation contains scalar `while`,
`conditional`, and `call` ops on XLA:GPU, and allow `PriorityFusion` to fuse
`map` with surrounding elementwise producers and consumers into a single `kLoop`
kernel:

1. **MLIR function partitioning (`computation_partitioner.cc`)**:
   When lowering a `kLoop` fusion to MLIR, `ComputationPartitioner` turns each
   HLO computation into MLIR helper functions. Previously it only visited
   computations called directly by the fusion (such as a `map` or `reduce` body)
   and assumed their parameters and results were single scalars. It now:
   - Walks `called_computations()` transitively so `while` bodies/conditions,
     `conditional` branches, and `call` targets nested inside `map` also get
     MLIR functions.
   - Flattens tuple parameters and results on subgraphs (including nested tuples
     and empty `()` tuples) into one MLIR argument or return value per flattened
     leaf.
   - Simplifies `PartitionedComputation`'s subgraph metadata construction around
     each partitioned subgraph's single post-order root (handling empty-tuple
     `()` roots with zero index dimensions, while multi-root subgraphs remain
     handled by `Subgraph::ForEpilogue`).
   - Returns `Undefined` operand indexing for control-flow ops, internal tuples,
     and tuple-returning `get-tuple-element`s in `ComputeOperandIndexingMaps`,
     since `indexing_analysis.cc` only models array-indexed ops.

2. **MLIR op emission (`elemental_hlo_to_mlir.cc`)**:
   Represents scalar-leaf tuples as flat lists of scalar MLIR values (slicing
   leaf ranges in `EmitParameter` and `EmitGetTupleElement`), and adds emitters
   translating scalar `call` to `xla.pure_call`, scalar `while` to `scf.while`,
   and scalar `conditional` to `scf.if` (for `pred[]`) or `scf.index_switch`
   (for integer branch indices).

3. **GPU fusion (`priority_fusion.cc`, `gpu_fusible.cc`)**:
   Allow `PriorityFusion` to fuse `map` with elementwise producers and
   consumers, disable loop unrolling for fusions containing `map`, and update
   `GetFusibleComputations` so fusion passes do not run inside `while` or
   `conditional` computations that are nested inside a `map` (which already
   executes inside a single kernel).

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Cap the number of operands of a loop fusion

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Cap the number of operands of a loop fusion

`CpuInstructionFusion` has no bound on how large a loop fusion may grow. The only size-related guard, `FusionNodeIndexingEvaluation::CodeDuplicationTooHigh`, is skipped entirely when the pass runs with `may_duplicate=false`, which `cpu_compiler.cc` selects whenever `xla_cpu_use_multi_output_fusion` is set.

On reverse-mode AD programs of stencil codes (Enzyme-MLIR / Reactant differentiating the Oceananigans ocean model) this produces loop fusions with 210–250 operands and 880–1045 fused instructions per output element: the `pad`-accumulate chain of every halo'd adjoint pulls in each stencil tap's whole producer DAG. The elemental emitter's per-element code for such a fusion neither vectorizes nor fits in registers; the reverse loop ran ~10× the primal while doing 4.2× its FLOPs.

This change adds an operand budget, checked independently of `may_duplicate()`: a producer is not fused into an existing fusion if the result would have more than `xla_cpu_max_fusion_operands` distinct operands (default 96, matching the GPU backend's `MaxOperandsAndOutputsPerFusion`). The option is an `xla_backend_extra_options` entry read through `cpu_options`; a value `<= 0` disables the check.

The budget is deliberately on operands only. An earlier revision also capped the number of fused instructions (512), which split long single-input elementwise chains and changed numerics in two JAX CPU tests: (a) `jax.scipy.special.iv` (f32) is a 540-instruction chain using double-float arithmetic; XLA:CPU sets `contract` on all FP arithmetic, so a kernel boundary prevents FMA contraction across it and breaks the error-free transformations (1.36 ULP instead of ≤ 1). (b) `ndtri_exp` gradient (bf16) differs on subnormal inputs: XLA:CPU runs kernels with denormals-are-zero, but LLVM folds `y == 0` on a bf16→f32 convert into an integer test on the bits, while `y < 0` stays a `ucomiss` that honors DAZ; which fold applies depends on the kernel boundaries. Both effects are pre-existing properties of XLA:CPU that any change in fusion boundaries can expose; the operand cap alone does not split these chains (they have 1–13 operands) and does not change either test.

Measurements (Oceananigans channel-model gradient, 8 time steps, one x86 core, `xla_cpu_use_multi_output_fusion` on; min / median of 3 calls):

| operand cap | gradient | primal |
|---|---|---|
| unpatched | 28.1 / 28.9 s | 3.01 s |
| disabled (`0`, control) | 28.0 / 29.3 s | — |
| 128 | 17.4 / 17.7 s | — |
| 96 (default) | 13.8 / 14.2 s | 2.89 s |
| 64 | 14.8 / 14.9 s | — |
| 48 | 11.7–13.1 / 12.2–13.2 s | 2.37 s |
| 32 | 12.8 / 13.1 s | 2.19 s |

(The 48 row spans four runs with the earlier instruction cap at 512, 1024, 4096 and disabled: 13.0, 11.7, 12.8, 13.1 s min — the instruction cap had no measurable effect, which is why it was dropped.) Results are bit-identical in the objective and agree with the unpatched build to rel. L2 ≤ 2e-15 in every gradient field.

The default is 96 rather than 48 based on a sweep over a suite of 80 CPU benchmark HLO models (A/B against head, 20 runs each). Compiling every model at several caps shows that any cap from 48 to 128 changes the fused HLO of the same two models (every other model has at most 42 operands per fusion), whereas the TORAX plasma-simulation models have fusions of 49–267 operands and are sensitive to the exact value: at cap 48 three of them regress 2–5% in wall time on Granite Rapids (4–13% on AMD Rome), while at cap 96 none regresses by more than 1% and their geomean improves by 1.2% (Granite Rapids) / 2.6% (Rome). The two models affected at any cap are within ±2% at either value. Suite-wide, the cap leaves runtime unchanged (geomean −0.2%) and improves compile wall time by 2% at the cost of 2% more compile CPU time.

Tests: `cpu_instruction_fusion_test` gains five cases on a 120-tap pad/add chain: the default budget splits it (largest fusion exactly 96 operands), also with `may_duplicate=false`, the budget is configurable (16), disabling it fuses the whole chain into one fusion, and a malformed option value is rejected with `InvalidArgument`.

The same change is vendored as a patch in Enzyme-JAX (https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Enzyme-JAX/pull/3882, https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Enzyme-JAX/pull/3883).

display_title: [XLA] Guard ScanLoopAccumulatorInputUnification against live uses

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Guard ScanLoopAccumulatorInputUnification against live uses

`ScanLoopAccumulatorInputUnification` replaces uses of `input_gte_inner` inside
the inner scan loop body with the accumulator `acc` and rewrites the inner loop
init tuple so the accumulator slot receives the input buffer. Previously,
`FindAccumulatorInputPairs` and `UnifyAccumulatorWithInput` did not verify:

1. That `gte_user` (`dynamic-update-slice`) has a single user, does not read
   `acc` as its update operand, and appears only once in the inner body root
   tuple, and that `input_gte_inner` appears only once in the inner body root
   tuple.
2. That all `body_param` users are `get-tuple-element`, that the GTEs for
   `param_idx` and `input_idx_inner` are unique, and that the non root user of
   `input_gte_inner` is selected explicitly.
3. That all `while_instr` users are `get-tuple-element` with
   `tuple_index() != input_idx_inner`, that `while_init()` has a single user
   and is not the parent root, and that the parent computation has a `tuple`
   root and is a `while_body()`.

Enforce these invariants before unifying an accumulator with an input.

display_title: [XLA] Do not inline `map` computations rooted at control-flow instructions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Do not inline `map` computations rooted at control-flow instructions.

`MapInliner` currently skips `kFusion` roots when all operands are parameters,
but still tries to clone control-flow roots (`CallContext::kControlFlow`, such
as `kWhile`, `kConditional`, and `kCall`) directly to the tensor shape of the
enclosing `map`. Cloning those instructions to a non-scalar shape produces
invalid HLO (and for `while`, tensor-wide loop termination does not match
per-element `map` semantics). Skip inlining them as well.

display_title: [XLA] Remove unnecessary `CallContext::kControlFlow` checks in `HloLivenessAnalysis`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Remove unnecessary `CallContext::kControlFlow` checks in `HloLivenessAnalysis`.

`PropagateLivenessToParameterCallers` and `PropagateLivenessThroughControlFlow`
already check each caller instruction's opcode (`kWhile`, `kCall`,
`kConditional`), so gating them on
`call_graph_node.context() == CallContext::kControlFlow` had no reason to be
there. Worse, when a `while`, `call`, or `conditional` is nested inside an
embedded computation such as `map`, `CallGraph` marks its callee computations
`CallContext::kEmbedded` (or `kBoth` if shared), so the check suppressed
liveness propagation to the caller and let `HloModuleDCE` treat live
loop-carried tuple elements as dead.

display_title: [XLA] Avoid propagating or querying tile counts on `{unreduced}` shardings

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Avoid propagating or querying tile counts on `{unreduced}` shardings

`IsLeafShardingMoreSpecific` previously checked `IsManualLeaf()` and `IsReplicatedOrSingleDeviceLeaf()` before calling `NumTiles()`, hitting `CHECK(IsTiledLeaf())` in `TiledDataRank()` when encountering `{unreduced}` (or `{unknown}`) leaf shardings during `PickRepresentativeOperand`. In addition, `IsSpatiallyPartitioned` and `ReturnImprovedShardingImpl` did not exclude unreduced shardings, allowing GSPMD `ShardingPropagation` to treat `{unreduced}` operands as spatially partitioned candidates for arbitrary operations.

Guard `IsLeafShardingMoreSpecific`, `ReturnImprovedShardingImpl`, `UntileLeafShape`, `IsSpatiallyPartitioned`, and `PickRepresentativeOperand` against unreduced and unknown shardings so they neither crash on `NumTiles()` nor propagate `{unreduced}` across unsupported operations while still allowing valid tiled operands to propagate.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/50824.

head_commit.message:
In `HandleScatterWithoutConflicts`, SPMD partitioning lowers conflict free `scatter` operations by masking nonzero shard operands to the reduction identity and reducing across partitions. Previously, `HandleScatterWithoutConflicts` computed `index_passthrough_dims` via `GetGatherScatterIndexPassThroughDims`, which subtracts `GetScatterParallelBatchDims` and excludes batch dimensions whose `scatter_indices` come from `iota` or constants.

When `scatter_indices` and `updates` are sharded along an axis where the operand is unsharded, excluding `iota` dimensions skipped masking and `AllReduceAlongShardingDims`. Each partition then kept only its local shard of scatter updates.

Compute `index_passthrough_dims` in `HandleScatterWithoutConflicts` with `GetGatherConnectedDimsAcrossIndicesAndOutput` so every implicit batch dimension outside `scatter_indices_batching_dims` participates in identity masking and `AllReduceAlongShardingDims`. Explicit batching scatters and conflict resolving scatters are unchanged.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Synchronize single-block phases via block barriers.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Synchronize single-block phases via block barriers.

Phased nodes in `ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion` previously emitted a cluster barrier at every phase boundary and configured even pure single-block fusions as 1-block thread-block clusters. When consecutive phases each execute on a single block (`bid == 0`), cluster barriers pay unnecessary GPC barrier latency and flush SM L1 cache lines that would otherwise stay hot across phases.

Group contiguous runs of single-block phases under a shared `bid < 1` guard and synchronize transitions between single-block phases with a block barrier outside any thread-count guard. When every phase in a phased node uses a single block, omit cluster launch dimensions so pure single-block fusions launch without a thread-block cluster.

head_commit.message:
PR #51724: [XLA:GPU] Add locality-domain placement to the CUDA device allocator

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51724

📝 Summary of Changes

Implements the allocator layer that later PRs build the per-domain BFC pools on.

display_title: In `HandleScatterWithoutConflicts`, SPMD partitioning lowers conflict free `scatter` operations by masking nonzero shard operands to the reduction identity and reducing across partitions. Previously, `HandleScatterWithoutConflicts` computed `index_passthrough_dims` via `GetGatherScatterIndexPassThroughDims`, which subtracts `GetScatterParallelBatchDims` and excludes batch dimensions whose `scatter_indices` come from `iota` or constants.

head_commit.message:
In `HandleScatterWithoutConflicts`, SPMD partitioning lowers conflict free `scatter` operations by masking nonzero shard operands to the reduction identity and reducing across partitions. Previously, `HandleScatterWithoutConflicts` computed `index_passthrough_dims` via `GetGatherScatterIndexPassThroughDims`, which subtracts `GetScatterParallelBatchDims` and excludes batch dimensions whose `scatter_indices` come from `iota` or constants.

When `scatter_indices` and `updates` are sharded along an axis where the operand is unsharded, excluding `iota` dimensions skipped masking and `AllReduceAlongShardingDims`. Each partition then kept only its local shard of scatter updates.

Compute `index_passthrough_dims` in `HandleScatterWithoutConflicts` with `GetGatherConnectedDimsAcrossIndicesAndOutput` so every implicit batch dimension outside `scatter_indices_batching_dims` participates in identity masking and `AllReduceAlongShardingDims`. Explicit batching scatters and conflict resolving scatters are unchanged.

display_title: [XLA] Guard ScanLoopAccumulatorInputUnification against live uses

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Guard ScanLoopAccumulatorInputUnification against live uses

`ScanLoopAccumulatorInputUnification` replaces uses of `input_gte_inner` inside
the inner scan loop body with the accumulator `acc` and rewrites the inner loop
init tuple so the accumulator slot receives the input buffer. Previously,
`FindAccumulatorInputPairs` and `UnifyAccumulatorWithInput` did not verify:

1. That `gte_user` (`dynamic-update-slice`) has a single user, does not read
   `acc` as its update operand, and appears only once in the inner body root
   tuple, and that `input_gte_inner` appears only once in the inner body root
   tuple.
2. That all `body_param` users are `get-tuple-element`, that the GTEs for
   `param_idx` and `input_idx_inner` are unique, and that the non root user of
   `input_gte_inner` is selected explicitly.
3. That all `while_instr` users are `get-tuple-element` with
   `tuple_index() != input_idx_inner`, that `while_init()` has a single user
   and is not the parent root, and that the parent computation has a `tuple`
   root and is a `while_body()`.

Enforce these invariants before unifying an accumulator with an input.

display_title: [XLA] Handle late bound async-start DUS in the async chain output path

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Handle late bound async-start DUS in the async chain output path

Dataflow analysis crashes on a late bound `async-start` wrapping `dynamic-update-slice`. Such a start has no operands; its operands and output are bound on the `async-update`. `UpdateAsyncStartValueSet` special cased the DUS start and read `operand(0)` without the bound and shape checks that `UpdateAsyncChainOutputValueSet` applies to every other async op.

The DUS case now lives in `UpdateAsyncChainOutputValueSet`: a start wrapping `dynamic-update-slice` takes its output values from its destination operand instead of the wrapped root, and a start without operands is skipped. The existing bound checks cover a start whose output is not bound yet. Early bound starts keep their behavior.

[XLA:SPMD] Lower `@CustomSPMDPartitioning` in Shardy when GSPMD is skipped.

When Shardy generates shard-local device code (`CONVERT_GLOBAL_TO_LOCAL` without GSPMD), custom calls registered via JAX `@custom_partitioning` (such as `@CustomSPMDPartitioning`) previously reached codegen unlowered because only GSPMD invoked their partitioning callbacks. display_title: [XLA] Remove unnecessary `CallContext::kControlFlow` checks in `HloLivenessAnalysis`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Remove unnecessary `CallContext::kControlFlow` checks in `HloLivenessAnalysis`.

`PropagateLivenessToParameterCallers` and `PropagateLivenessThroughControlFlow`
already check each caller instruction's opcode (`kWhile`, `kCall`,
`kConditional`), so gating them on
`call_graph_node.context() == CallContext::kControlFlow` had no reason to be
there. Worse, when a `while`, `call`, or `conditional` is nested inside an
embedded computation such as `map`, `CallGraph` marks its callee computations
`CallContext::kEmbedded` (or `kBoth` if shared), so the check suppressed
liveness propagation to the caller and let `HloModuleDCE` treat live
loop-carried tuple elements as dead.

display_title: [XLA] Do not inline `map` computations rooted at control-flow instructions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Do not inline `map` computations rooted at control-flow instructions.

`MapInliner` currently skips `kFusion` roots when all operands are parameters,
but still tries to clone control-flow roots (`CallContext::kControlFlow`, such
as `kWhile`, `kConditional`, and `kCall`) directly to the tensor shape of the
enclosing `map`. Cloning those instructions to a non-scalar shape produces
invalid HLO (and for `while`, tensor-wide loop termination does not match
per-element `map` semantics). Skip inlining them as well.

display_title: [XLA] HloComputationDeduplicator: keep call targets apart from other callees

head_commit.message:
[XLA] HloComputationDeduplicator: keep call targets apart from other callees

📝 Summary of Changes

HloComputationDeduplicator keys computations by their canonical text and merges duplicates no matter how they are called. Since fa5295919d, HloDataflowAnalysis requires that a computation with a kCall caller has only kCall callers (it treats call targets like inlined code) and CHECKs it in IsRegularCallComputation. So when a non-inlined call target and, for example, a while body have the same text, the deduplicator merges them and the next dataflow analysis (the collective pipeliner on GPU) aborts the compiler.

This change adds a marker to the dedup key when a computation has a kCall caller, so call targets only merge with other call targets and the rest only with the rest. The pass already keeps computations called by collectives apart in the same spirit. Identical call targets still get deduplicated.

🎯 Justification

Fixes #50970. The module from the issue (a call with inlineable="false" to a negate computation feeding a while whose body is the same negate) aborts GPU compilation at HEAD with "Check failed: !is_regular_call_computation || absl::c_all_of(node.caller_callsites(), ...)" from hlo_dataflow_analysis.cc. With this change it compiles and runs. CPU is not affected because its pipeline only runs the deduplicator in the multi-module driver.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:

Two new tests in xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers/hlo_computation_deduplicator_test.cc:
- DontDeduplicateCallTargetWithWhileBody: the issue's module, expects no change and both computations kept. Fails without the fix (the while body is removed).
- DeduplicateIdenticalCallTargets: two inlineable="false" calls to identical computations are still merged into one.

Not covered on purpose: merging an embedded callee (map/reduce body) with a control-flow callee (while/conditional body) is also possible and gives HloDataflowAnalysis's clean Unimplemented "called in both a parallel and sequential context" error rather than a crash; keying on the call context would prevent that too, happy to extend if wanted.

🧪 Execution Tests:

None added. Checked manually with run_hlo_module

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019350903
