display_title: [XLA] Avoid propagating or querying tile counts on `{unreduced}` shardings

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Avoid propagating or querying tile counts on `{unreduced}` shardings

`IsLeafShardingMoreSpecific` previously checked `IsManualLeaf()` and `IsReplicatedOrSingleDeviceLeaf()` before calling `NumTiles()`, hitting `CHECK(IsTiledLeaf())` in `TiledDataRank()` when encountering `{unreduced}` (or `{unknown}`) leaf shardings during `PickRepresentativeOperand`. In addition, `IsSpatiallyPartitioned` and `ReturnImprovedShardingImpl` did not exclude unreduced shardings, allowing GSPMD `ShardingPropagation` to treat `{unreduced}` operands as spatially partitioned candidates for arbitrary operations.

Guard `IsLeafShardingMoreSpecific`, `ReturnImprovedShardingImpl`, `UntileLeafShape`, `IsSpatiallyPartitioned`, and `PickRepresentativeOperand` against unreduced and unknown shardings so they neither crash on `NumTiles()` nor propagate `{unreduced}` across unsupported operations while still allowing valid tiled operands to propagate.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/50824.

head_commit.message:
Add two disabled reproduction tests to `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cupti_tracer_test.cc` (with cross-context CUDA helpers in `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cuda_test.h` and `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cuda_test.cu.cc`) covering the CUPTI AB-BA deadlock during `PrepareForProfilerStart` (`cuptiSubscribe` / `cuptiSubscribe_v2`):

1. `CuptiTracerTest.DISABLED_ConcurrentCrossContextStreamCaptureDuringSubscribeDeadlocks`: runs a peer-waiting kernel on one `CUcontext` while a worker thread captures and launches a signaling CUDA graph on a second `CUcontext` concurrently with `PrepareForProfilerStart`, reproducing the deadlock between CUPTI's per-context module initialization on the first context and CUPTI's temporary process-wide `CUPTI_API_ENTER` barrier across all contexts.
2. `CuptiTracerTest.DISABLED_ConcurrentCrossContextGraphLaunchDuringSubscribeDeadlocks`: reproduces the same `cuptiSubscribe` / `cuptiSubscribe_v2` barrier deadlock when CUDA graphs are pre-instantiated during warmup and the worker thread only executes `cuCtxSetCurrent` + `cuGraphLaunch` during steady-state execution (modeling `--xla_enable_command_buffers_during_profiling=true`).

Both tests are prefixed with `DISABLED_` so the test target passes by default in CI, while running manually with `--test_arg=--gunit_also_run_disabled_tests` (or `--test_arg=--gtest_also_run_disabled_tests` in OSS) reproduces the failures.

head_commit.message:
Add two disabled reproduction tests to `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cupti_tracer_test.cc` (with cross-context CUDA helpers in `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cuda_test.h` and `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cuda_test.cu.cc`) covering the CUPTI AB-BA deadlock during `PrepareForProfilerStart` (`cuptiSubscribe` / `cuptiSubscribe_v2`):

1. `CuptiTracerTest.DISABLED_ConcurrentCrossContextStreamCaptureDuringSubscribeDeadlocks`: runs a peer-waiting kernel on one `CUcontext` while a worker thread captures and launches a signaling CUDA graph on a second `CUcontext` concurrently with `PrepareForProfilerStart`, reproducing the deadlock between CUPTI's per-context module initialization on the first context and CUPTI's temporary process-wide `CUPTI_API_ENTER` barrier across all contexts.
2. `CuptiTracerTest.DISABLED_ConcurrentCrossContextGraphLaunchDuringSubscribeDeadlocks`: reproduces the same `cuptiSubscribe` / `cuptiSubscribe_v2` barrier deadlock when CUDA graphs are pre-instantiated during warmup and the worker thread only executes `cuCtxSetCurrent` + `cuGraphLaunch` during steady-state execution (modeling `--xla_enable_command_buffers_during_profiling=true`).

Both tests are prefixed with `DISABLED_` so the test target passes by default in CI, while running manually with `--test_arg=--gunit_also_run_disabled_tests` (or `--test_arg=--gtest_also_run_disabled_tests` in OSS) reproduces the failures.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Synchronize single-block phases via block barriers.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Synchronize single-block phases via block barriers.

Phased nodes in `ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion` previously emitted a cluster barrier at every phase boundary and configured even pure single-block fusions as 1-block thread-block clusters. When consecutive phases each execute on a single block (`bid == 0`), cluster barriers pay unnecessary GPC barrier latency and flush SM L1 cache lines that would otherwise stay hot across phases.

Group contiguous runs of single-block phases under a shared `bid < 1` guard and synchronize transitions between single-block phases with a block barrier outside any thread-count guard. When every phase in a phased node uses a single block, omit cluster launch dimensions so pure single-block fusions launch without a thread-block cluster.

display_title: [IFRT Proxy] Validate array specs of client-supplied RemapPlans on the server.

head_commit.message:
[IFRT Proxy] Validate array specs of client-supplied RemapPlans on the server.

`IfrtBackend::HandleRemapArraysRequest` deserialized the `RemapPlan` sent by
the proxy client and passed it to `Client::RemapArrays()` without validating
it. Whether an inconsistent plan was rejected therefore depended on the IFRT
implementation behind the server, and not all of them check it. PjRt-IFRT, for
example, does not compare the input and output array specs of a plan, so a
plan whose output dtype or shape disagrees with its inputs produced arrays
whose metadata does not describe their buffers.

The server now calls `RemapPlan::ValidateArraySpecs()` right after
deserializing the plan and returns the error to the client. This checks the
array indices used by the plan and that mapped input and output arrays agree
on dtype, shard shape, memory kind and layout. It is the lightweight
validation that `RemapPlan` asks `Client::RemapArrays()` implementations to
perform at least, and its result is cached in the plan, so implementations
that validate again do not repeat the work. The slower shard-level checks of
`RemapPlan::Validate()` are not run per request and remain the responsibility
of the implementation.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019327894

display_title: PR #51724: [XLA:GPU] Add locality-domain placement to the CUDA device allocator

head_commit.message:
PR #51724: [XLA:GPU] Add locality-domain placement to the CUDA device allocator

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51724

📝 Summary of Changes

Implements the allocator layer that later PRs build the per-domain BFC pools on.

Adds `StreamExecutor::CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocator(int locality_domain_id)`, which returns a MemoryAllocator whose physical memory is placed on one locality domain (die) of a multi-die GPU.

CUDA implementation: `locality_domain_id` added to `CudaDeviceAllocator::Options`. When it's set, the allocator creates physical memory with `cuMemCreate` with location set to `CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE_LOCALITY_DOMAIN`.

Errors instead of fallback: it rejects out-of-range domain IDs, CUDA older than 13.4, single-domain devices, and the cuMemAlloc path (use_vmm=false). It never falls back to whole-device memory.

🎯 Justification

This is the third PR in the locality-domain series ([first](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50131) and [second](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51429) PRs)

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature and 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A: this PR adds the allocator only. Performance benefits to be evaluated later.

🧪 Unit Tests:
- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.RejectsOutOfRangeLocalityDomain`: domain IDs below -1 or above 255 are rejected.
- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.LocalityDomainRequiresCuda134`: CUDA older than 13.4 is rejected.
- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.LocalityDomainRequiresVmm`: use_vmm=false is rejected.
- `CudaExecutorTest.CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocatorRejectsInvalidId`: IDs outside [0, domain_count) are rejected.
- `DeviceAddressVmmAllocatorTest.RejectsLocalityDomainMemorySpaces`: locality-domain colors are rejected on every allocation path.

🧪 Execution Tests:
Both run on a single GPU:

- `CudaDeviceAllocatorLocalityDomainTest.PlacesMemoryOnEachDomain`: for each domain, allocates memory and checks with `cuMemGetAllocationPropertiesFromHandle` that its location is `CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE_LOCALITY_DOMAIN` with the requested domain ID. Then it round-trips data host to device to host.
- `CudaExecutorTest.CreateLocalityDomainMemoryAllocatorWorks`: creates an allocator for every domain and allocates from it. On a single-domain GPU, it checks that creating one fails.
Copybara import of the project:

--

display_title: In `HandleScatterWithoutConflicts`, SPMD partitioning lowers conflict free `scatter` operations by masking nonzero shard operands to the reduction identity and reducing across partitions. Previously, `HandleScatterWithoutConflicts` computed `index_passthrough_dims` via `GetGatherScatterIndexPassThroughDims`, which subtracts `GetScatterParallelBatchDims` and excludes batch dimensions whose `scatter_indices` come from `iota` or constants.

head_commit.message:
In `HandleScatterWithoutConflicts`, SPMD partitioning lowers conflict free `scatter` operations by masking nonzero shard operands to the reduction identity and reducing across partitions. Previously, `HandleScatterWithoutConflicts` computed `index_passthrough_dims` via `GetGatherScatterIndexPassThroughDims`, which subtracts `GetScatterParallelBatchDims` and excludes batch dimensions whose `scatter_indices` come from `iota` or constants.

When `scatter_indices` and `updates` are sharded along an axis where the operand is unsharded, excluding `iota` dimensions skipped masking and `AllReduceAlongShardingDims`. Each partition then kept only its local shard of scatter updates.

Compute `index_passthrough_dims` in `HandleScatterWithoutConflicts` with `GetGatherConnectedDimsAcrossIndicesAndOutput` so every implicit batch dimension outside `scatter_indices_batching_dims` participates in identity masking and `AllReduceAlongShardingDims`. Explicit batching scatters and conflict resolving scatters are unchanged.

display_title: [XLA] HloComputationDeduplicator: keep call targets apart from other callees

head_commit.message:
[XLA] HloComputationDeduplicator: keep call targets apart from other callees

📝 Summary of Changes

HloComputationDeduplicator keys computations by their canonical text and merges duplicates no matter how they are called. Since fa5295919d, HloDataflowAnalysis requires that a computation with a kCall caller has only kCall callers (it treats call targets like inlined code) and CHECKs it in IsRegularCallComputation. So when a non-inlined call target and, for example, a while body have the same text, the deduplicator merges them and the next dataflow analysis (the collective pipeliner on GPU) aborts the compiler.

This change adds a marker to the dedup key when a computation has a kCall caller, so call targets only merge with other call targets and the rest only with the rest. The pass already keeps computations called by collectives apart in the same spirit. Identical call targets still get deduplicated.

🎯 Justification

Fixes #50970. The module from the issue (a call with inlineable="false" to a negate computation feeding a while whose body is the same negate) aborts GPU compilation at HEAD with "Check failed: !is_regular_call_computation || absl::c_all_of(node.caller_callsites(), ...)" from hlo_dataflow_analysis.cc. With this change it compiles and runs. CPU is not affected because its pipeline only runs the deduplicator in the multi-module driver.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:

Two new tests in xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers/hlo_computation_deduplicator_test.cc:
- DontDeduplicateCallTargetWithWhileBody: the issue's module, expects no change and both computations kept. Fails without the fix (the while body is removed).
- DeduplicateIdenticalCallTargets: two inlineable="false" calls to identical computations are still merged into one.

Not covered on purpose: merging an embedded callee (map/reduce body) with a control-flow callee (while/conditional body) is also possible and gives HloDataflowAnalysis's clean Unimplemented "called in both a parallel and sequential context" error rather than a crash; keying on the call context would prevent that too, happy to extend if wanted.

🧪 Execution Tests:

None added. Checked manually with run_hlo_module

head_commit.message:
[TF] Switch TensorFlow default build to Bzlmod and sync MODULE.bazel.

Following the Bazel 8.8.2 upgrade, enable `--enable_bzlmod` and `--noenable_workspace` by default in TensorFlow while adding `--config=workspace` as a fallback configuration and flipping `ci/official/envs/bzlmod` to `--config workspace` so `WORKSPACE` continues to be tested in CI for downstream consumers. Also set `--experimental_repository_downloader_retries=5` and `common --experimental_downloader_config=bazel_downloader.cfg` (including BCR mirror fallback rules), add `--nobuild_runfile_links` to `common:rbe_base`, prepend Bzlmod canonical CUDA library paths to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` in `test:linux_cuda_13_wheel_test`, and disable `layering_check` on macOS (`common:macos`) to match Linux and Windows toolchains.

In `MODULE.bazel`, third-party Bzlmod extensions, and platform patches:
- Register the hermetic SYCL and ROCm C++ toolchains from `rules_ml_toolchain`, sync the CUDA, CCCL (`3.4.0`), NCCL (`nccl_redist_patched`), NVSHMEM, SYCL, local sysroot, and `libdrm` module extensions and XLA third-party repositories (including deduplicating `nccl_archive`, `nvtx_archive`, `png`, and `absl_py` from `tf_third_party`) with XLA's `MODULE.bazel` and `workspace2.bzl`, and align the root BCR module declarations (`pybind11_bazel` 3.0.0, `apple_support` 2.8.0, `rules_swift` 2.9.0, `googletest` 1.18.0, `highway` 1.4.0, `dev_dependency = True` on test-only modules `rules_webtesting`, `fuzztest`, and `libprotobuf-mutator`, and `repo_name = None` compatibility pins for `c-ares`, `eigen`, `grpc-java`, and `libpfm`).
- Configure multi-platform `pip.parse` wheels (`xla_pypi = "pypi"`, `local_wheels` overrides via `rules_python_local_wheel.patch`, `@pypi//{}:whl` in `tf_wheel.bzl`, and Python 3.14 freethreaded lockfile/platform support), `pythons_hub`, `python_version_repo` via `use_repo_rule` (with `REQUIREMENTS` lockfile support, `TF_PYTHON_VERSION` fallback, `-freethreaded`/`-ft` suffix handling, and removing the unused `python_version_ext` extension), reproducible module extensions (`reproducible = True` on `third_party_ext`, `googleapis_ext`, and `nccl_redist_ext`), `maven`, and Bzlmod Java repositories (`generated_rule_name` in `java_repos.bzl` and Guava/JSR305/ErrorProne repos), alias `@system_python//:python_headers` to `rules_python`'s hermetic headers in `bazel9.patch`, and update `nvidia_wheel_deps`, `requirements_lock_3_*.txt` (`protobuf==6.33.6`), and `code_check_full.bats` for Bzlmod.
- Add Bzlmod compatibility patch overrides (`pybind11_abseil.patch`, Windows DLL support in `protobuf/bazel9.patch`, `google_cloud_cpp.patch`, `rules_android.patch`, and `googletest:remove_alwayslink.patch`), update Windows protobuf symbol exports in `_pywrap_tensorflow.def`, and update `gpu_prim.h` and `where_op_gpu.cu.h` (`THRUST_VERSION >= 300200`) for CCCL 3.4.0 compatibility.

Follow-up CLs will clean up remaining legacy WORKSPACE artifacts and deprecated `BUILD.oss` `$(location)` make variables, migrate remaining `java_import_external` and `tf_third_party` repositories to BCR modules/`rules_jvm_external`, and re-enable Bazel 8 incompatible flags in `.bazelrc`.

display_title: [XLA] Avoid propagating or querying tile counts on `{unreduced}` shardings

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Avoid propagating or querying tile counts on `{unreduced}` shardings

`IsLeafShardingMoreSpecific` previously checked `IsManualLeaf()` and `IsReplicatedOrSingleDeviceLeaf()` before calling `NumTiles()`, hitting `CHECK(IsTiledLeaf())` in `TiledDataRank()` when encountering `{unreduced}` (or `{unknown}`) leaf shardings during `PickRepresentativeOperand`. In addition, `IsSpatiallyPartitioned` and `ReturnImprovedShardingImpl` did not exclude unreduced shardings, allowing GSPMD `ShardingPropagation` to treat `{unreduced}` operands as spatially partitioned candidates for arbitrary operations.

Guard `IsLeafShardingMoreSpecific`, `ReturnImprovedShardingImpl`, `UntileLeafShape`, `IsSpatiallyPartitioned`, and `PickRepresentativeOperand` against unreduced and unknown shardings so they neither crash on `NumTiles()` nor propagate `{unreduced}` across unsupported operations while still allowing valid tiled operands to propagate.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/50824.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Handle root GemmFusion outputs like any other output.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Handle root GemmFusion outputs like any other output.

GemmFusion special-cased a fusion output that is the root of its computation: it set the new root by hand and removed the old instruction instead of calling `ReplaceInstruction`. Every other output goes through `ReplaceInstruction`, which also carries the replaced instruction's frontend attributes, metadata and control dependencies over to the replacement. The fusion, or the bitcast that replaces the output, therefore inherited those only when the replaced instruction was not the root.

`ReplaceInstruction` already updates the computation root, so the special case is not needed. Remove it so that root and non-root outputs are replaced the same way.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Run stream-annotated computations on locality domains

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Run stream-annotated computations on locality domains

A call annotated with _xla_stream_annotation="locality_domain:<id>" is
wrapped into an async region by ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapper and
assigned LocalityDomainStreamId(<id>) by ExecutionStreamAssignment, so it
runs on that domain's stream. The wrapper rejects locality-domain regions
that contain collectives, send/recv or nested stream annotations, and
AsyncStartThunk::Prepare rejects communication thunks inside them at
runtime. Stream annotations are kept only on the call, not on the
get-tuple-elements that unpack a multi-result call.

Add two disabled reproduction tests to `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cupti_tracer_test.cc` (with cross-context CUDA helpers in `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cuda_test.h` and `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cuda_test.cu.cc`) covering the CUPTI AB-BA deadlock during `PrepareForProfilerStart` (`cuptiSubscribe` / `cuptiSubscribe_v2`):

2. `CuptiTracerTest.DISABLED_ConcurrentCrossContextGraphLaunchDuringSubscribeDeadlocks`: reproduces the same `cuptiSubscribe` / `cuptiSubscribe_v2` barrier deadlock when CUDA graphs are pre-instantiated during warmup and the worker thread only executes `cuCtxSetCurrent` + `cuGraphLaunch` during steady-state execution (modeling `--xla_enable_command_buffers_during_profiling=true`).

display_title: [XLA] Avoid propagating or querying tile counts on `{unreduced}` shardings

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Avoid propagating or querying tile counts on `{unreduced}` shardings

`IsLeafShardingMoreSpecific` previously checked `IsManualLeaf()` and `IsReplicatedOrSingleDeviceLeaf()` before calling `NumTiles()`, hitting `CHECK(IsTiledLeaf())` in `TiledDataRank()` when encountering `{unreduced}` (or `{unknown}`) leaf shardings during `PickRepresentativeOperand`. In addition, `IsSpatiallyPartitioned` and `ReturnImprovedShardingImpl` did not exclude unreduced shardings, allowing GSPMD `ShardingPropagation` to treat `{unreduced}` operands as spatially partitioned candidates for arbitrary operations.

Guard `IsLeafShardingMoreSpecific`, `ReturnImprovedShardingImpl`, `UntileLeafShape`, `IsSpatiallyPartitioned`, and `PickRepresentativeOperand` against unreduced and unknown shardings so they neither crash on `NumTiles()` nor propagate `{unreduced}` across unsupported operations while still allowing valid tiled operands to propagate.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/50824.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [IFRT Proxy] Validate array specs of client-supplied RemapPlans on the server.

head_commit.message:
[IFRT Proxy] Validate array specs of client-supplied RemapPlans on the server.

`IfrtBackend::HandleRemapArraysRequest` deserialized the `RemapPlan` sent by
the proxy client and passed it to `Client::RemapArrays()` without validating
it. Whether an inconsistent plan was rejected therefore depended on the IFRT
implementation behind the server, and not all of them check it. PjRt-IFRT, for
example, does not compare the input and output array specs of a plan, so a
plan whose output dtype or shape disagrees with its inputs produced arrays
whose metadata does not describe their buffers.

The server now calls `RemapPlan::ValidateArraySpecs()` right after
deserializing the plan and returns the error to the client. This checks the
array indices used by the plan and that mapped input and output arrays agree
on dtype, shard shape, memory kind and layout. It is the lightweight
validation that `RemapPlan` asks `Client::RemapArrays()` implementations to
perform at least, and its result is cached in the plan, so implementations
that validate again do not repeat the work. The slower shard-level checks of
`RemapPlan::Validate()` are not run per request and remain the responsibility
of the implementation.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019020697

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Synchronize single-block phases via block barriers.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Synchronize single-block phases via block barriers.

Phased nodes in `ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion` previously emitted a cluster barrier at every phase boundary and configured even pure single-block fusions as 1-block thread-block clusters. When consecutive phases each execute on a single block (`bid == 0`), cluster barriers pay unnecessary GPC barrier latency and flush SM L1 cache lines that would otherwise stay hot across phases.

Group contiguous runs of single-block phases under a shared `bid < 1` guard and synchronize transitions between single-block phases with a block barrier outside any thread-count guard. When every phase in a phased node uses a single block, omit cluster launch dimensions so pure single-block fusions launch without a thread-block cluster.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] HostOffloader: do not follow tokens when walking host memory offload paths

head_commit.message:
[XLA] HostOffloader: do not follow tokens when walking host memory offload paths

📝 Summary of Changes

HostOffloader::WalkDownHostMemoryOffloadPaths follows the offloaded buffer through its users. For a generic user it keeps the same shape index, so a send user is tracked as the whole send result tuple, its send-done user is tracked as a token, and if that token is returned from the entry computation the pass ends up in the output streaming check, which does CHECK(leaf.has_layout()) on the entry result leaves. Tokens never have a layout, so the compiler aborts.

A token carries no data, so an offloaded buffer never flows through it (send-done only produces a token; the data stays in send's output {0}). This change skips token-shaped successors in the walk, and makes the output streaming check skip non-array leaves (the send result tuple itself has a token leaf, so returning the send from the entry computation hit the same CHECK). Arrays and tuples are handled exactly as before, and the existing send test (BasicHostTransferSendNoCrash) still gets its copy to host memory in front of the send.

🎯 Justification

Fixes #50971. The module from the issue (MoveToHost -> send -> send-done -> ROOT tuple(send-done)) aborts GPU compilation at HEAD with "Check failed: leaf.has_layout() Expecting output shape of entry computation to have a layout." With this change it gets the same clean error as the module without the MoveToHost ("Expected recv to match send", the fuzzer module has no matching recv), and a properly paired program compiles normally.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:

Two new tests in xla/hlo/transforms/host_offloader_test.cc. SendDoneTokenReturnedFromEntryNoCrash runs the pass on the issue's module and checks that it succeeds, that the root is still tuple(send-done(send(copy(param), after-all))), that the copy is in host memory and the parameter is not, and that no annotations remain. SendResultReturnedFromEntryNoCrash returns the send itself from the entry computation and expects a clean error (the offloaded data would be returned in a device memory output). Without the source change both tests abort with the CHECK from the issue.

🧪 Execution Tests:

None added. Checked manually with run_hlo_module

display_title: Reject negative mesh axis indices in AxisRef::Validate

head_commit.message:
Reject negative mesh axis indices in AxisRef::Validate

`AxisRef::Validate` only checked that the mesh axis index is less than the
number of mesh axes, so a negative index, e.g. one read from an `AxisRefProto`,
passed validation. `NamedSharding` and `MeshAxesReplicaGroupList` rely on this
validation in their constructors and afterwards use the index to look up mesh
axis sizes, which resulted in an out-of-bounds read.

`AxisRef::Validate` now also returns `InvalidArgument` for negative indices.
Both constructors already `CHECK` the validation result, so a negative index is
now rejected before it is used as an index.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [CHLO] Do not recompose composites with a mismatched region count

head_commit.message:
[CHLO] Do not recompose composites with a mismatched region count

`ChloOpRecomposePattern` moves the regions of a `stablehlo.composite` into the
CHLO op it creates by zipping both region lists with `llvm::zip_equal`.
`stablehlo.composite` accepts any number of regions, while the CHLO ops have a
fixed number, and nothing checked that the two agree. `zip_equal` only asserts
on equal lengths; without assertions it iterates over the composite's regions,
so a composite with more regions than the CHLO op made the pattern access
regions past the end of the new op, and one with fewer left the new op with an
empty region.

Compare the region counts before moving the regions and fail the match when
they differ, erasing the op that was just created so the IR is left unchanged.
Such a composite is then left in place, like any other composite that the
pass does not recompose.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1019015280

display_title: [XLA] Drop removed instructions from the HloCSE representative set

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Drop removed instructions from the HloCSE representative set

HloCSE can remove an instruction that it has already recorded as the
representative of its equivalence class: a duplicate iota operand of the
instruction being visited, or an operand that becomes unused when a duplicate
instruction is replaced. The removed instruction stayed in the set, so an
equivalent instruction visited later was replaced with it. That left live
instructions with an operand that is no longer part of the computation and
that is deleted when the module is cleaned up.

Erase such instructions from the set before they are removed. The extra
lookup only happens for instructions that HloCSE removes in addition to the
duplicate it is replacing, so the common path is unchanged.

display_title: [XLA] Bounds-check table lookup indices in collective_opt_utils

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Bounds-check table lookup indices in collective_opt_utils

The collective pattern matchers evaluate table lookups, i.e. a dynamic-slice
of a rank-1 constant indexed by a device id or by another table lookup, at
compile time. The index was only checked for being non-negative before it was
used to read the constant's literal, and the literal accessors only validate
indices with `DCHECK`. A module whose replica groups or tables yield an index
past the end of a table therefore caused an out-of-bounds read in optimized
builds.

Route all four table reads (`GetIndexForId`, `IsPerIdOffsets`,
`EvaluateOffset` and `GetIndicesSpecForDynamicSlice`) through a single
`GetTableEntry` helper that returns `nullopt` when the index is outside the
constant table, so that the pattern simply does not match. Lookups into iota
tables are unchanged since they do not read a literal.

display_title: [TF] Switch TensorFlow default build to Bzlmod and sync MODULE.bazel.

head_commit.message:
[TF] Switch TensorFlow default build to Bzlmod and sync MODULE.bazel.

Following the Bazel 8.8.2 upgrade, enable `--enable_bzlmod` and `--noenable_workspace` by default in TensorFlow while adding `--config=workspace` as a fallback configuration and flipping `ci/official/envs/bzlmod` to `--config workspace` so `WORKSPACE` continues to be tested in CI for downstream consumers. Also set `--experimental_repository_downloader_retries=5` and `common --experimental_downloader_config=bazel_downloader.cfg` (including BCR mirror fallback rules), add `--nobuild_runfile_links` to `common:rbe_base`, prepend Bzlmod canonical CUDA library paths to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` in `test:linux_cuda_13_wheel_test`, and disable `layering_check` on macOS (`common:macos`) to match Linux and Windows toolchains.

- Register the hermetic SYCL and ROCm C++ toolchains from `rules_ml_toolchain`, sync the CUDA, CCCL (`3.4.0`), NCCL (`nccl_redist_patched`), NVSHMEM, SYCL, local sysroot, and `libdrm` module extensions and XLA third-party repositories (including deduplicating `nccl_archive`, `nvtx_archive`, `png`, and `absl_py` from `tf_third_party`) with XLA's `MODULE.bazel` and `workspace2.bzl`, and align the root BCR module declarations (`pybind11_bazel` 3.0.0, `apple_support` 2.8.0, `rules_swift` 2.9.0, `googletest` 1.18.0, `highway` 1.4.0, `dev_dependency = True` on test-only modules `rules_webtesting`, `fuzztest`, and `libprotobuf-mutator`, and `repo_name = None` compatibility pins for `c-ares`, `eigen`, `grpc-java`, and `libpfm`).

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Cap the number of operands of a loop fusion

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Cap the number of operands of a loop fusion

`CpuInstructionFusion` has no bound on how large a loop fusion may grow. The only size-related guard, `FusionNodeIndexingEvaluation::CodeDuplicationTooHigh`, is skipped entirely when the pass runs with `may_duplicate=false`, which `cpu_compiler.cc` selects whenever `xla_cpu_use_multi_output_fusion` is set.

On reverse-mode AD programs of stencil codes (Enzyme-MLIR / Reactant differentiating the Oceananigans ocean model) this produces loop fusions with 210–250 operands and 880–1045 fused instructions per output element: the `pad`-accumulate chain of every halo'd adjoint pulls in each stencil tap's whole producer DAG. The elemental emitter's per-element code for such a fusion neither vectorizes nor fits in registers; the reverse loop ran ~10× the primal while doing 4.2× its FLOPs.

This change adds an operand budget, checked independently of `may_duplicate()`: a producer is not fused into an existing fusion if the result would have more than `xla_cpu_max_fusion_operands` distinct operands (default 96, matching the GPU backend's `MaxOperandsAndOutputsPerFusion`). The option is an `xla_backend_extra_options` entry read through `cpu_options`; a value `<= 0` disables the check.

The budget is deliberately on operands only. An earlier revision also capped the number of fused instructions (512), which split long single-input elementwise chains and changed numerics in two JAX CPU tests: (a) `jax.scipy.special.iv` (f32) is a 540-instruction chain using double-float arithmetic; XLA:CPU sets `contract` on all FP arithmetic, so a kernel boundary prevents FMA contraction across it and breaks the error-free transformations (1.36 ULP instead of ≤ 1). (b) `ndtri_exp` gradient (bf16) differs on subnormal inputs: XLA:CPU runs kernels with denormals-are-zero, but LLVM folds `y == 0` on a bf16→f32 convert into an integer test on the bits, while `y < 0` stays a `ucomiss` that honors DAZ; which fold applies depends on the kernel boundaries. Both effects are pre-existing properties of XLA:CPU that any change in fusion boundaries can expose; the operand cap alone does not split these chains (they have 1–13 operands) and does not change either test.

Measurements (Oceananigans channel-model gradient, 8 time steps, one x86 core, `xla_cpu_use_multi_output_fusion` on; min / median of 3 calls):

| operand cap | gradient | primal |
|---|---|---|
| unpatched | 28.1 / 28.9 s | 3.01 s |
| disabled (`0`, control) | 28.0 / 29.3 s | — |
| 128 | 17.4 / 17.7 s | — |
| 96 (default) | 13.8 / 14.2 s | 2.89 s |
| 64 | 14.8 / 14.9 s | — |
| 48 | 11.7–13.1 / 12.2–13.2 s | 2.37 s |
| 32 | 12.8 / 13.1 s | 2.19 s |

(The 48 row spans four runs with the earlier instruction cap at 512, 1024, 4096 and disabled: 13.0, 11.7, 12.8, 13.1 s min — the instruction cap had no measurable effect, which is why it was dropped.) Results are bit-identical in the objective and agree with the unpatched build to rel. L2 ≤ 2e-15 in every gradient field.

The default is 96 rather than 48 based on a sweep over a suite of 80 CPU benchmark HLO models (A/B against head, 20 runs each). Compiling every model at several caps shows that any cap from 48 to 128 changes the fused HLO of the same two models (every other model has at most 42 operands per fusion), whereas the TORAX plasma-simulation models have fusions of 49–267 operands and are sensitive to the exact value: at cap 48 three of them regress 2–5% in wall time on Granite Rapids (4–13% on AMD Rome), while at cap 96 none regresses by more than 1% and their geomean improves by 1.2% (Granite Rapids) / 2.6% (Rome). The two models affected at any cap are within ±2% at either value. Suite-wide, the cap leaves runtime unchanged (geomean −0.2%) and improves compile wall time by 2% at the cost of 2% more compile CPU time.

Tests: `cpu_instruction_fusion_test` gains five cases on a 120-tap pad/add chain: the default budget splits it (largest fusion exactly 96 operands), also with `may_duplicate=false`, the budget is configurable (16), disabling it fuses the whole chain into one fusion, and a malformed option value is rejected with `InvalidArgument`.

The same change is vendored as a patch in Enzyme-JAX (https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Enzyme-JAX/pull/3882, https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Enzyme-JAX/pull/3883).

display_title: [XLA] HloComputationDeduplicator: keep call targets apart from other callees

head_commit.message:
[XLA] HloComputationDeduplicator: keep call targets apart from other callees

📝 Summary of Changes

HloComputationDeduplicator keys computations by their canonical text and merges duplicates no matter how they are called. Since fa5295919d, HloDataflowAnalysis requires that a computation with a kCall caller has only kCall callers (it treats call targets like inlined code) and CHECKs it in IsRegularCallComputation. So when a non-inlined call target and, for example, a while body have the same text, the deduplicator merges them and the next dataflow analysis (the collective pipeliner on GPU) aborts the compiler.

This change adds a marker to the dedup key when a computation has a kCall caller, so call targets only merge with other call targets and the rest only with the rest. The pass already keeps computations called by collectives apart in the same spirit. Identical call targets still get deduplicated.

🎯 Justification

Fixes #50970. The module from the issue (a call with inlineable="false" to a negate computation feeding a while whose body is the same negate) aborts GPU compilation at HEAD with "Check failed: !is_regular_call_computation || absl::c_all_of(node.caller_callsites(), ...)" from hlo_dataflow_analysis.cc. With this change it compiles and runs. CPU is not affected because its pipeline only runs the deduplicator in the multi-module driver.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:

Two new tests in xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers/hlo_computation_deduplicator_test.cc:
- DontDeduplicateCallTargetWithWhileBody: the issue's module, expects no change and both computations kept. Fails without the fix (the while body is removed).
- DeduplicateIdenticalCallTargets: two inlineable="false" calls to identical computations are still merged into one.

Not covered on purpose: merging an embedded callee (map/reduce body) with a control-flow callee (while/conditional body) is also possible and gives HloDataflowAnalysis's clean Unimplemented "called in both a parallel and sequential context" error rather than a crash; keying on the call context would prevent that too, happy to extend if wanted.

🧪 Execution Tests:

None added. Checked manually with run_hlo_module

display_title: Chunk sub-tile unpacking in tiled delinearizer.

head_commit.message:
Chunk sub-tile unpacking in tiled delinearizer.

Delinearizing sub-tile-packed tensors previously allocated an unpacked host buffer spanning the entire array before transposing into the output literal. Large packed arrays caused tens of gigabytes of unreserved host memory growth.

This change unpacks and transposes sub-tile-packed device-to-host data in bounded megabyte-scale chunks above the scratch threshold. Each chunk reuses small scratch storage and uses parallel transpose execution whenever the chunk plan exposes parallelism.

display_title: [GPU][ROCm] Request exportable (POSIX fd) handles for VMM allocations

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] Request exportable (POSIX fd) handles for VMM allocations

Collective libraries share buffers by exporting their allocation handles
as POSIX file descriptors, but ROCm VMM allocations were created with
hipMemHandleTypeNone, which permits no export at all.

Add RocmVmmAllocator::Options with an `enable_posix_fd_handle` flag and
thread it through every ROCm VMM site, centralizing the property setup
and granularity query in GetRocmVmmAllocationParams(). The four sites
previously built properties by hand, risking a granularity queried with
properties that differ from the ones used to allocate; a reservation and
the allocations mapped into it must agree on it. The ROCm
DeviceAddressVmmAllocator::Create() factory opts in, since that allocator
also serves collective memory.

Exportable handles are requested only on ROCm 10.0+ (HIP 7.15+); earlier
runtimes cannot export and import them correctly, so the request is
dropped with a warning rather than failing the allocation.

Add rocm_vmm_exportable_handles_test, covering the option in both
directions, an export/import round trip, and a collective-space buffer
from the kVmm allocator.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Add ShapeTracker::TryGetStridedView().

`TryGetStridedView()` returns, for every output dimension of the tracker, the
segments (strides and extents) of the input that the dimension iterates over.
Broadcasted segments have stride 0, and a dimension can span several segments,
e.g. when a reshape merges two dimensions that were transposed apart. It
returns std::nullopt if the tracked transformation is not a strided view of the
input, i.e. if materializing it would require a copy or a reduction.

This will be used to compute the sizes and strides of the tensors of cuDNN GEMM
fusions (see cl/1017387793).

display_title: PR #52725: [XLA:GPU] Expose ROCm's libhipcxx from include/hipccl as its own include root

head_commit.message:
PR #52725: [XLA:GPU] Expose ROCm's libhipcxx from include/hipccl as its own include root

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52725

Motivation
As part of the move to the CCCL 3.0-3.3 API, AMD is introducing hipCCL, a
unified package for rocPRIM, hipCUB and rocThrust that mirrors the role
NVIDIA's CCCL plays for CUB, Thrust and libcu++. hipCCL installs libhipcxx under `<rocm>/include/hipccl`, which Bazel did not expose, so hipCUB could fail with 'libhipcxx could not be found'.

📝 Summary of Changes
This change works with both the legacy and the new (upcoming) hipccl layouts. It adds `:rocm_libhipcxx_includes`, which strips `include/hipccl` so the headers
are reachable by hipCUB, and depends on it from `:rocm_headers_includes`.

The glob covers the whole directory rather than naming subdirectories, because
libhipcxx headers cross-reference each other across cuda/, hip/, nv/ and
amd/. `allow_empty` leaves ROCm installs without `include/hipccl` unchanged.

🎯 Justification
This change is important to avoid build failures with ROCm's planned migration to hipCCL 3.x.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
N/A

🧪 Unit Tests:
Tested by building XLA in two ROCm containers:
- libhipcxx alone under include/hipccl, with hipCUB/rocPRIM/rocThrust in
include/
- the hipCCL layout, where hipCUB/rocPRIM/rocThrust are under include/hipccl too and include/{hipcub,rocprim,rocthrust} are symlinks into it

No unit tests were added.

🧪 Execution Tests:
N/A

Reviewed and approved for AMD by the ROCm XLA team in ROCm/xla#1419.
Copybara import of the project:

--
67fb5b65f46510c6f6e150ce2d3a605ac911a2cc by amd-mcieslak <323359018+amd-mcieslak@users.noreply.github.com>:

[ROCm] Expose libhipcxx from include/hipccl as its own include root

hipCCL3 installs libhipcxx under <rocm>/include/hipccl, which Bazel did not
expose, so hipCUB users failed with 'libhipcxx could not be found'. Works

head_commit.message:
PR #52725: [XLA:GPU] Expose ROCm's libhipcxx from include/hipccl as its own include root

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52725

Motivation
As part of the move to the CCCL 3.0-3.3 API, AMD is introducing hipCCL, a
unified package for rocPRIM, hipCUB and rocThrust that mirrors the role
NVIDIA's CCCL plays for CUB, Thrust and libcu++. hipCCL installs libhipcxx under `<rocm>/include/hipccl`, which Bazel did not expose, so hipCUB could fail with 'libhipcxx could not be found'.

📝 Summary of Changes
This change works with both the legacy and the new (upcoming) hipccl layouts. It adds `:rocm_libhipcxx_includes`, which strips `include/hipccl` so the headers
are reachable by hipCUB, and depends on it from `:rocm_headers_includes`.

The glob covers the whole directory rather than naming subdirectories, because
libhipcxx headers cross-reference each other across cuda/, hip/, nv/ and
amd/. `allow_empty` leaves ROCm installs without `include/hipccl` unchanged.

🎯 Justification
This change is important to avoid build failures with ROCm's planned migration to hipCCL 3.x.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
N/A

🧪 Unit Tests:
Tested by building XLA in two ROCm containers:
- libhipcxx alone under include/hipccl, with hipCUB/rocPRIM/rocThrust in
include/
- the hipCCL layout, where hipCUB/rocPRIM/rocThrust are under include/hipccl too and include/{hipcub,rocprim,rocthrust} are symlinks into it

No unit tests were added.

🧪 Execution Tests:
N/A

Reviewed and approved for AMD by the ROCm XLA team in ROCm/xla#1419.
Copybara import of the project:

display_title: Chunk sub-byte sub-tile packing in tiled linearizer.

head_commit.message:
Chunk sub-byte sub-tile packing in tiled linearizer.

Linearizing sub-byte sub-tile-packed tensors previously allocated an unpacked host buffer spanning the entire array. Large sub-byte arrays caused tens of gigabytes of unreserved host memory growth.

This change transposes and repacks sub-byte host-to-device data in bounded megabyte-scale chunks above the scratch threshold. Each chunk reuses small scratch storage and uses parallel transpose execution whenever the chunk plan exposes parallelism.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Log all evaluated and rejected tiling candidates in GpuPerformanceModelWithIndexingAnalysis.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Log all evaluated and rejected tiling candidates in GpuPerformanceModelWithIndexingAnalysis.

This helps in debugging how we end up choosing particular tiles.

Log `TilingSpace` and top-K candidates at `VLOG(2)` and remaining sorted
candidates plus root-prefixed rejection reasons at `VLOG(3)` in
`gpu_indexing_performance_model.cc`.

`--xla_gpu_dump_cost_model_top_k_candidates_to` runs after `candidates` is
truncated to `top_k` and omits rejected tilings and `TilingSpace` details.
Because fusion passes call `TryFindBestTilingForFusionAsync` with `top_k=1`
(only the autotuner passes `top_k > 1`), the dump flag records only the winning
tiling during fusion-stage evaluations.
